docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

While generalist vision-language-action (VLA) models have enabled diverse open-world manipulation, real-world robotic assistance requires two critical capabilities they currently lack: personalization and reliable execution. First, executing an instruction like "make me a sandwich" requires grounding subtask decomposition in persistent user preferences rather than relying on a single generic solution. Second, reliable deployment demands explainable safety assurance that proactively prevents hazards and gracefully recovers from occasional physical failures. To address these gaps, we present CarryOn, a dual-loop harness designed to augment a frozen VLA policy. The planning loop maintains persistent user-level and scene-level context that is continually grounded against new observations and revised through interaction, enabling personalized task selection and execution grounding across conversations and changing scenes. The execution loop actively supervises policy rollouts, shielding actions from predicted hazardous contact. When execution fails, the system invokes reusable control-based recovery skills that restore task progress and are refined through reflection on earlier failures. On a real robot and in simulation, CarryOn dispatches preference-consistent subtasks across users and scenes, reduces the violation rate of an already safety-finetuned VLA from 52.6% to 6.1%, and increases recovery success from 13% to 80% when refined skills are reused.

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Reliable contact-rich manipulation requires detecting execution deviations early enough for corrective action. Yet most monitoring methods are reactive, identifying anomalies only after they become observable. Anticipating such anomalies is challenging because visual observations only partially reveal physical interaction, while planned actions describe intended motion rather than their actual physical consequences. We address this problem with MAIA, a multimodal framework for anomaly anticipation. Its vision-action-force world model learns nominal interaction dynamics and predicts the visual and force responses of planned actions, while a lightweight anomaly head predicts impending interaction anomalies. To enable systematic evaluation, we introduce CRIA, a real-world multimodal dataset of 2,852 trajectories spanning 18 contact-rich manipulation tasks, with frame-level annotations of anomaly onset and evolution. Experiments on both seen and novel tasks show that MAIA achieves more accurate anomaly discrimination than representative baselines while providing earlier warnings, with bACC scores of 0.765 and 0.710 and median anticipation lead times of 28.0 and 25.1 steps, respectively. Moreover, using these predictions for anomaly-aware action selection improves end-to-end task success from 52.6% to 61.5% without retraining the underlying manipulation policy. These results highlight the value of modeling future physical consequences for proactive anomaly anticipation.

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Imitation learning enables robots to perform complex tasks by leveraging human-collected demonstrations. However, most existing approaches require labor-intensive data collection with additional teleoperation systems, which hinders scalability. Human videos represent a natural source of data that implicitly contain knowledge of manipulation behaviors. However, transferring them to robots remains challenging due to the visual domain gap and the absence of explicit action labels. In this work, we introduce TDV, a trajectory-based framework that leverages data generation to enable generalizable manipulation. TDV focuses on task-relevant objects by leveraging plug-and-play 6D pose estimation techniques to extract object trajectories from human videos, thereby mitigating the impact of irrelevant backgrounds and varying viewpoints. As a modality-agnostic intermediate representation, trajectories are inherently independent of the visual domains and different embodiments, enabling efficient data generation. Our method outperforms previous approaches on RLBench simulation tasks, achieving near 100\% success rates across seven tasks. In real-world experiments, TDV enables cross-embodiment generalization manipulation from one-shot human demonstrations by leveraging efficient trajectory generation techniques.

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Vision-language-action (VLA) policies are typically trained with action prediction as the primary supervision signal, since robots ultimately execute actions. Auxiliary objectives such as latent-action (LA) and future-vision (FV) prediction are often added to improve policy learning, yet they compete with action prediction for the same training budget. We ask whether, under a fixed budget, allocating a substantial share of training samples to such objectives, rather than to further action prediction, can improve policy learning. We build a unified VLA framework that couples a two-stream multimodal diffusion transformer (MMDiT) with a sample-level router, which assigns each training sample to either action prediction or an auxiliary objective and thus makes supervision allocation explicit. Within this framework, we instantiate three LA targets based on LAPA and its DINO-feature variants, and three FV targets based on DINOv3, V-JEPA 2, and Wan2.2 representations. Across LIBERO, CALVIN, and four real-robot tasks, suitable LA and FV supervision outperforms action-only training under the same budget, even when action prediction receives no more than half of the training samples. FV generally outperforms LA, although the strongest LA target remains competitive on CALVIN. Diagnostic analyses suggest that DINO-based LA targets emphasize relative motion, whereas FV targets emphasize absolute position and task identity. We therefore argue that what robot policies learn to predict, and how training is allocated among these targets, should be treated as explicit design choices rather than defaulting to action-dominant training.

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Many vision-language-action policies rely on action-labeled robot demonstrations and lack an explicit mechanism for predicting future visual states. These limitations hinder learning from action-free videos and can encourage overfitting to demonstration conditions, weakening generalization and robustness. We present TS-WAM, a lightweight Teacher-Student World-Action Model that addresses these challenges through self-supervised temporal learning and explicit future prediction. Its vlm-jepa framework learns from heterogeneous data, including robot demonstrations and action-free human videos, using an EMA target branch without requiring a separately trained external teacher. By coupling vlm-jepa with delta-lwm, TS-WAM learns to predict latent actions from the current observation and instruction and uses them to predict future visual features that guide action generation at inference. A unified end-to-end training architecture jointly optimizes temporal representation learning, visual dynamics, and robot control without a separate latent-action or world-model pretraining stage. The EMA target branch is removed at inference, keeping the deployed policy lightweight. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and SimplerEnv, together with real-world manipulation experiments on Franka Research 3 and RevoTron, demonstrate that TS-WAM achieves strong manipulation performance, generalization, and robustness.

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Flow-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies are inherently stochastic: different noise seeds can produce action chunks of varying quality from the same observation. At test time, however, the policy typically commits to a single sample without an explicit estimate of its quality. In fine-grained manipulation, executing a suboptimal action can irreversibly disrupt task progress and lead to failure. To exploit policy stochasticity, we introduce a training-free two-axis trigger that uses two initial samples to measure within-chunk temporal variation and cross-sample variance, detecting the critical states. Once triggered, a JEPA-based latent world model ranks candidate action chunks by predicting action-conditioned future latent states and the corresponding changes in task progress. By operating in latent space, the verifier avoids pixel reconstruction and enables efficient and more accurate ranking. Across three real-world tasks, $\textit{i.e.,}$ pen insertion, pipetting, and apple placement), our method raises the average completion score from 50.8% to 65.5%, while adding 326 ms for sampling and verification per triggered decision on a single RTX 4090. Consistent gains are also observed in simulation, where the average success rate rises from 66.4% to 73.6% in the clean setting of RoboTwin 2.0, from 62.8% to 69.6% in its randomized setting, and from 96.9% to 97.6% on LIBERO.

docs.text:
复制原文

Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models present a promising paradigm for general-purpose robot manipulation, but closed-loop deployment is often limited by inference efficiency: at each timestep, high-resolution, often multi-view images are encoded into hundreds of visual tokens that dominate transformer computation and latency. Token compression via attention is a natural solution but is challenging for VLA control because (1) decision-critical tokens are determined by the task, not generic visual saliency, and (2) the token budget varies substantially across steps, so static metrics and budgets waste computation or discard control-critical tokens. We introduce FastVLA, a training-free, task-aware, and temporally adaptive visual token compression framework. At each step, FastVLA scores token importance via task-to-vision attention and adaptively sets the compression rate from the importance-distribution uniformity, measured by an inverse-Simpson metric with online sliding-window calibration. We evaluate FastVLA on OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, and CogACT across LIBERO and SIMPLER, and on a physical Franka Research 3 robot. In simulation, it reduces LLM-backbone FLOPs by 35-59\% and action latency by 9-32\% (a 1.09$\times$-1.46$\times$ speedup) while maintaining task success, achieving a comparable or better efficiency-performance trade-off than existing plug-and-play token compression/pruning/reuse baselines. On the real robot, it cuts end-to-end latency by 20\% (1.25$\times$ speedup) at comparable success. Code is available at https://github.com/jiuyixu25/FastVLA.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

VLA 与策略学习记忆与技能

首发 2026-10-15（UTC）｜近7天补收  ·  收录于 2026-10-17 日报

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

We introduce REKI, a 2.4B vision-language-action model (VLA) pretrained exclusively on public data that sets a new Pareto frontier between performance and model size: on LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin Clean2Rand and RoboCasa365, it is outperformed only by models about twice its size. REKI consists of a vision-language model (VLM) followed by a flow-matching action expert, and is pretrained on a curated mixture of public robot, egocentric human and vision-language data. Additionally, we endow it with a memory that gives the policy access to its recent past at negligible cost: a few register tokens in the action expert summarise the output of the VLM at each frame and persist in the expert's cache. This memory improves success in simulation and on real robots, and makes oscillations between poses about four times rarer. REKI uses a simple model design and training paradigm, and is optimised to be efficient at training and inference. We release the full code across data curation, training, inference and evaluation, deployment, and all pretrained and finetuned model weights: https://github.com/kyutai-labs/reki.

MOSS — Mode-Oriented Source Shaping for Robot Flow Matching Policies

其他具身方向

首发 2026-10-15；版本：v1。补收原因：近 7 天未推送，直接研究操作策略的行为选择；作为邻近方法收录。  ·  收录于 2026-10-20 日报

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

In robotic manipulation, the same observation often admits multiple feasible actions. Generative policies such as diffusion and flow matching naturally capture such multimodal behaviors, yet which mode is executed is left to random sampling and cannot be actively controlled. We propose Mode-Oriented Source Shaping (MOSS), which turns mode selection into an explicit choice of where generation starts. We first reveal, both empirically and theoretically, that deterministic flow transport induces mode-dependent structure in the source space. Under ideal deterministic ODE transport, distinct behavioral modes have distinct source-space preimages, while practical approximation errors can blur their boundaries due to imbalanced data, limited model capacity, and few inference steps. Motivated by this source-space structure, MOSS constructs semantically aligned mode-specific Gaussian sources that encode mode identity in the initial noise. A modality-strength estimator predicts the local degree of multimodality, which adaptively controls the geometry of the mode-specific sources. It contracts them toward a shared Gaussian where behaviors are similar and separates them near behavioral branching points. During deployment, the desired behavior is selected at inference simply by sampling from the corresponding component. Across 6 simulated and 3 real-world manipulation tasks, MOSS steers to the target mode up to 100% of the time with high task success, recovers minority modes at over 90% guidance rate under a 10:90 imbalance dataset, and surpasses mode-conditioned flow policy by 43.3 points of guidance rate on real robots.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: 核心贡献
docs.text: 将不同操作模式对应到不同初始噪声分布，并按当前状态的多模态程度调整分布间距，使“选择哪种做法”成为可控采样步骤。

docs.title: 关键实验
docs.text: Galaxea R1 Lite 右臂完成摆杯、取蔬菜、开抽屉；每个指定模式 20 次。摆杯总成功率约 98%，模式条件 FM 为 70%；两种模式的“成功且符合指定模式”比例为 95%／100%，对照为 15%／85%。

docs.title: 重要边界
docs.text: 上述模式指标包含任务成功，不能解释为单纯分类准确率。需要训练示范的模式标签；开抽屉总成功率约 83%，低于对照 85%，收益并非普遍提高完成率。实机只控制机械臂，不构成移动操作；仿真任务集合还含纯导航。

docs.title: Mem4Act
docs.text:
Mem4Act: Learning Effective Latent Memory for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation

VLA 与策略学习记忆与技能

首发 2026-10-15（UTC）｜近7天补收  ·  收录于 2026-10-18 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗GitHub ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

作者仓库当前以说明文档、许可或展示资源为主，未发现实现代码。 （2026-10-21 核查）

贡献：核心方法｜路线：VLA｜层级：策略学习、观测记忆｜任务：桌面单臂/双臂操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Long-horizon robotic manipulation fundamentally requires memory: agents must retain task-relevant information from past observations and interactions and use it to guide future actions. Existing approaches typically preserve raw historical observations, compressed visual tokens, or language summaries, but these representations either expose the action policy to increasingly long histories or risk discarding task-relevant temporal, semantic, and perceptual information. We introduce Mem4Act, a framework for learning effective latent memory as a fixed-size representation explicitly optimized for long-horizon robotic control. Mem4Act addresses three coupled challenges: how to efficiently cover long histories, what information memory should retain, and how to ensure the policy actually relies on memory. To this end, it organizes history via multi-granularity temporal aggregation, preserves complementary semantic and perceptual information through question-answering supervision and key-frame DINO feature reconstruction, and employs memory-first two-stage training to encourage greater use of memory by the action policy. The resulting memory captures both high-level task state and fine-grained perceptual evidence while providing a bounded interface to the action policy. Across RoboMME, RMBench, and four real-world manipulation tasks, Mem4Act achieves state-of-the-art performance on memory-dependent control, with success rates of 49.88%, 61.0%, and 81.5%, respectively. Extensive ablations further demonstrate the importance of temporal aggregation, complementary memory supervision, and memory-first training.

docs.text: PAPER NOTE · 精选 03

docs.title: Spark-0
docs.text:
Spark-0: Scaling Spatially Aligned Tactile Pretraining for Robot Dexterous Manipulation

VLA 与策略学习

首发 2026-10-15（UTC）｜近7天补收  ·  收录于 2026-10-17 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗GitHub ↗GitHub ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

贡献：核心方法＋数据＋基准｜路线：VLA/VTLA｜层级：策略学习、接触感知｜任务：固定工作区双臂灵巧操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Generalist robot policies benefit from large-scale visual pretraining but often struggle with contact-rich dexterous manipulation, where force, compliance, and incipient slip are hard to observe from images. We present Spark-0, a spatially aligned vision-tactile-language-action (VTLA) model that uses touch in two complementary ways. During pretraining, image-space contact maps derived from tactile gloves, together with features from a frozen 3D geometry teacher, supervise the visual tokens; these objectives are removed at inference. In parallel, a tactile pathway encodes regional force histories and 3D taxel states to condition the action expert. A single checkpoint therefore supports both vision-only and tactile-conditioned deployment. To scale this supervision, we build HumanTouch, a 1,000-hour dataset of full-hand tactile human manipulation, and pretrain Spark-0 on it together with egocentric video, robot data, and simulation. We also release SparkArena, which pairs vision-only simulated tasks with tactile-conditioned real-robot tasks on one dexterous embodiment. Spark-0 achieves the highest mean success rate on both SparkArena tracks and ranks first on all eight aggregate metrics of the Ego Humanoid Manipulation Benchmark. Compared with vision-only pretraining on the same data and compute with touch discarded, retaining the touch of 1,000 hours of HumanTouch raises vision-only success on Ego Humanoid from 52.5% to 71.7%, and success on SparkArena-Real, where touch is also used at deployment, from 44.0% to 52.0%, indicating that touch serves not only as a policy input but also as scalable supervision for dexterous visuomotor pretraining. The Website is available at: https://xsparkai.com/Spark-0.

docs.text: PAPER NOTE · 精选 09

docs.title: T2-z
docs.text:
T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models

世界模型与 WAM

首发 2026-10-15（UTC）｜近7天补收  ·  收录于 2026-10-18 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗GitHub ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

贡献：核心方法｜路线：WM｜层级：环境适配、规划/动作选择｜任务：桌面操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. We introduce T2-Z for test-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions. This compact latent captures underlying environmental variation without supervision of what environmental factors exist or what values they take. During training, T2-Z alternates between two stages: a world-model optimization stage that fixes the latents and learns general action-conditioned dynamics across environments; and an environment-latent optimization stage that freezes the world model and optimizes the conditioning latents, allowing latent structure to emerge purely through world prediction. At test time, the world model remains frozen and a newly initialized environment latent is optimized from one or more test-time interactions, adapting the model to previously unseen environmental configurations. Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real-world robotic tasks, T2-Z reduces object prediction error metric from 15.20 to 7.00 and raises action success from 33.73% to 72.96%. Its emergent latents capture structured representations of individual and compounded factors across diverse visual scenes. Ablations further show that T2-Z can efficiently infer environment latents from as little as a single test-time interaction trajectory.

docs.text: PAPER NOTE · 精选 03

docs.title: VaM
docs.text:
Value as Memory: Online Value-Guided Post-training for General Robot Policies

VLA 与策略学习记忆与技能

首发 2026-10-15（UTC）｜近7天补收  ·  收录于 2026-10-18 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗GitHub ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

贡献：核心方法＋系统｜路线：VLA、在线RL｜层级：低层策略学习、进度记忆｜任务：桌面双臂操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Real-world post-training of generalist robot policies faces two challenges: partial observability makes action selection ambiguous, while offline post-training methods delay feedback from deployment experience. We present Value as Memory (VaM), a framework that addresses these challenges through value caching and online real-world reinforcement learning (RL). Value caching conditions actions on recent value predictions as task-progress memory, while online updates enable timely policy improvement by combining offline demonstrations, off-policy interventions, and on-policy rollouts for sample-efficient adaptation. As a result, VaM transitions from offline RL warmup to online autonomous learning with sparse rewards. Across long-horizon tasks involving deformable objects and contact-rich manipulation, VaM yields a mean absolute success-rate gain of $29.4\%$ with value caching, while achieving a $32.8\%$ gain with online autonomous learning over matched offline training. The evaluated online schedule performs $8\times$ as many policy iterations under the same gradient-step budget, with more than $2\times$ lower recorded time per gradient step with concurrent data collection and training.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

原归档未标版本，摘要采用 v1。

docs.text: 纸箱装配、衣物折叠、磁力积木装配三项长程实机任务，VaM最终三检查点成功率分别96.7%、88.9%、76.7%；去掉value caching后为81.7%、48.9%、43.3%，平均绝对增益29.4点。

docs.title: 重要局限
docs.text: 初始示范分别为200/90/30条，另有offline warmup和逐轮在线采集，并保留人工接管数据；结果是最终三检查点均值，训练交互成本较高，未证明跨任务零样本泛化。

新意不是普通critic，而是将在线价值估计显式反馈给动作策略作为部分可观测下的短期进度状态。

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Robot learning has advanced by scaling demonstration datasets and model capacity; however, deploying a new robot embodiment or task typically necessitates a dedicated teleoperation corpus. The resulting policies remain bounded by their imitation distributions, limiting generalization and continual self-improvement. We introduce RAX (Robot Agent eXploration), an open-source framework for robot agents centered on scaling exploration: enabling agents to improve by acquiring online experience and synthesizing executable programs. In RAX, a general-purpose coding agent generates robot control code, operating without action demonstration data, hand-engineered action primitives, or value-function guidance. Through online exploration, the agent identifies decision sequences that achieve task goals and compiles them into modular programs encapsulating the full perception-planning-control loop. Using RAX, we present a systematic multi-embodiment study on scaling online exploration across precision and long-horizon manipulation tasks using single-arm, bimanual, dexterous, mobile, and humanoid systems in simulation and on real robots. Generalization performance on unseen environments improves consistently as exploration scales. In simulation, RAX outperforms top baseline models by +37.4% on average. On real robots, RAX autonomously learns memory-dependent, articulated, high-precision, deformable, and long-horizon mobile manipulation tasks without human demonstrations, continually improving performance by composing verified skills from prior exploration sessions. As exploration scales, we observe emergent capabilities including active perception, error recovery, safety guardrails, and human-robot collaboration. We open-source RAX as a generalist robot-agent platform in which new robot embodiments are integrated through their APIs alone, without teleoperated data collection or policy training.

docs.title: MambaAct
docs.text:
MambaAct: Efficient Mamba Action Experts for Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Models

VLA 与策略学习

首发 2026-10-16（v1；补收）  ·  收录于 2026-10-19 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗GitHub ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

核心方法 + 模块/trick｜VLA｜低层控制/策略学习｜桌面操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong promise for generalist robotic manipulation, but their inference cost remains a major bottleneck for real-time control. This limitation is especially pronounced in flow-matching VLAs such as $π_{0.5}$, where the action expert is evaluated repeatedly during iterative denoising. We introduce MambaAct, an efficient Mamba action expert for flow-matching VLA policies. MambaAct retains the pretrained visual-language prefix encoder of $π_{0.5}$, while replacing its transformer-based action expert with a compact Mamba-based action expert. Within this expert, Mamba serves as the action mixer that models dependencies across the noisy continuous-action sequence. To preserve visual-language conditioning without repeated token-level cross-attention, MambaAct uses a lightweight Context Compressor to map Vision-language model (VLM) prefix tokens into a compact conditioning signal that gates and modulates each Mamba action block. MambaAct uses a $10\times$ smaller action expert and reduces flow-matching denoising latency by $64.8\%$ on LIBERO and $58.8\%$ in real-world deployment, while improving mean LIBERO success by $1.08$ percentage points across three independent fine-tuning seeds and maintaining gains on LIBERO-Plus and real-world benchmarks. Our code and model weights are publicly available at https://github.com/giakhuyendihoc/MambaAct.

docs.title: VLA-Fabric
docs.text:
VLA-Fabric: Learning Interaction for Composable Multi-Arm VLA Agents

VLA 与策略学习

首发 2026-10-16（v1；补收）  ·  收录于 2026-10-19 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗GitHub ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

核心方法 + 大系统｜VLA｜低层策略交互｜桌面多臂

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Vision-language-action (VLA) models are rapidly expanding what individual robots can accomplish, yet many real-world manipulation settings require multiple arms to operate as a coordinated system. Existing approaches organize multi-arm coordination in different ways, including centralized joint policies, high-level task or role assignment, and locally executed policies that react to teammates. However, how complete action-producing VLAs should explicitly interact with one another during action generation remains largely unexplored. We introduce VLA-Fabric, which organizes one complete VLA per arm while preserving local perception and action ownership, and enables coordination through learned interaction across policy boundaries. We first systematically study where such interaction should occur, how peer information should be aggregated, and how the interaction should be learned, revealing complementary coordination functions spanning shared context, peer-specific latent information, and action-stage interaction. We then re-instantiate these functions in a structurally different VLA architecture, showing that the coordination principle is not tied to a particular tensor layout or backbone implementation. Finally, we compose teams of three and four arms and evaluate them in simulation and physical experiments. On all four physical tasks, Full interaction improves success over independently trained local policies by 16--40 percentage points. Together, these results suggest that explicit interaction among complete VLA policies offers a scalable path toward networked embodied intelligence.

docs.title: SCOPE
docs.text:
SCOPE: Selective Certification of Program Edits for Embodied Heuristic Learning

智能体与程序学习移动操作

首发 2026-10-16（v1；补收）  ·  收录于 2026-10-19 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗GitHub ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

核心方法 + 大系统｜Agent / agentic coding｜规划/验证/恢复｜桌面 + 移动操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Embodied heuristic learning must balance strategic adaptation with the preservation of previously successful behavior. Local repairs may leave structural failures unresolved, whereas broader revisions can introduce regressions that are costly to detect through repeated environment interaction. We introduce SCOPE (Selective Certification Of Program Edits), which uses failed and successful executions as complementary evidence for program revision. Frontier-guided program search annotates a shared diagnostic graph with execution evidence to distinguish supported progress from unresolved checks. Selective behavioral certification uses stateful API replay to restore recorded responses and mutations, checking whether edits preserve selected historical successes. Diagnosis and certification feedback, supplemented by sparse environment diagnostics, guide consecutive repairs across configurations. SCOPE outperforms the strongest baseline in both simulation and real-world tasks. On LIBERO-PRO and Robosuite, it achieves mean success rates of 80.66% and 84.48%, with respective gains of 6.51 and 3.48 percentage points. Our code is available at https://github.com/VDIGPKU/SCOPE.

docs.text: PAPER NOTE · 精选 09

docs.title: ORD-WM
docs.text:
ORD-WM: Learning Object-Centric Rigid Dynamics for 3D World Modeling in Robotic Manipulation

世界模型与 WAM

首发 2026-10-16（v1；补收）  ·  收录于 2026-10-19 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

项目主页的 Code 按钮仍为占位链接，暂不展示为可用仓库。 （2026-10-21 核查）

核心方法｜WM/WAM｜低层规划/控制｜桌面操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

World models provide robots with a predictive mechanism for reasoning about how actions change object states in manipulation tasks. However, existing image-based and dense 3D world models do not explicitly impose object-level rigid motion, leaving rigid-object geometry preservation to be learned implicitly and making multi-step rollouts susceptible to shape drift or object-level motion inconsistency. To address this, we propose ORD-WM, a 3D world model that learns object-centric rigid dynamics for robotic manipulation. ORD-WM learns a vector-neuron variational autoencoder supervised by signed distance fields, which encodes each object point cloud as a geometry-aware latent representation composed of 3D vector features, and uses an action-conditioned dynamics model to predict object-wise SE(3) motion increments. Rather than generating unconstrained next latent states, ORD-WM analytically applies predicted object-wise rigid transformations to the current latent states, separating persistent object geometry from pose changes. Experiments show that ORD-WM enables stable, geometry-preserving multi-step prediction and supports efficient real-time replanning for closed-loop model predictive control in simulated and real-world manipulation scenarios.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.text: PAPER NOTE · 精选 08

docs.title: NestedVLA
docs.text:
NestedVLA: Learning to Consolidate and Generate Skills for Vision-Language-Action Models

VLA 与策略学习记忆与技能

首发 2026-10-16（v1；补收）  ·  收录于 2026-10-19 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗GitHub ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

核心方法｜VLA｜策略学习 + 技能层｜桌面操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models promise generalist robotic agents, yet consolidating skills learned across heterogeneous tasks and environments remains difficult: training data is fragmented across platforms, joint multi-task training suffers from interference, and model merging tends to introduce parameter conflicts or require architectural changes. We instead advocate a paradigm in which skills are first learned independently and then consolidated post hoc. To this end, we propose NestedVLA, which replaces parameter aggregation with parameter generation: a nested hypernetwork, conditioned on the target task, synthesizes task-adaptive action-expert parameters that compose with a frozen base VLA. Task-specific compressed VLM residuals are retained separately. This formulation enables flexible task-conditioned skill reuse while mitigating interference. Across three RL benchmarks (MetaWorld, ManiSkill, CALVIN), NestedVLA outperforms the strongest model-merging baseline by 41 pp on average, matches per-task fine-tuning within 1 pp on ManiSkill, and substantially closes the gap on CALVIN, pointing toward a storage-efficient route to skill consolidation. Code is available at https://github.com/WanyuGroup/NeurIPS2026-NestedVLA.

docs.text: PAPER NOTE · 精选 01

docs.title: LAW
docs.text:
LAW: Unifying Language, Action, and World Modeling for Agentic Physical Intelligence

VLA 与策略学习世界模型与 WAM智能体与程序学习记忆与技能

首发 2026-10-16（v1；补收）  ·  收录于 2026-10-19 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗GitHub ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

大系统｜VLA + WM/WAM + Agent｜技能/阶段 + 规划/观测/验证｜桌面双臂

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

World-action models jointly predict actions and future world states, but long-horizon manipulation further requires language reasoning to plan subtask objectives, assess execution progress, and guide action selection. We present LAW, a closed-loop VLM--WAM framework that unifies language reasoning, action generation, and world modeling through semantic subtask progress. Within the LAW agent, a hybrid-expert vision-language model plans the remaining subtasks, estimates the values of and fuses actions proposed by a world-action model, and asynchronously assesses execution status to support continued execution and subtask transitions. Within the world-action model, Mixture-of-Transformer Experts integrates modality-specific and shared computation for joint video--action modeling. Dual-stream hierarchical visual memory maintains temporal context for both models, while subtask-local value learning aligns action evaluation with semantic objectives and preserves supervision from successful prefixes of failed trajectories. LAW achieves 94.21% average success across 50 RoboTwin tasks. Replacing the WAM backbone with OpenWAM-$alpha$ further raises the average success rate to 95.56%, establishing a new open-source state of the art on RoboTwin. Despite having only 2B parameters, our VLM also outperforms variants using Embodied-R1.5 and GPT-5.5 High. On three long-horizon real-robot tasks, LAW achieves 65% average success, compared with 28.33% for $pi_{0.5}$ and 25% for Fast-WAM.

IMEP — Beyond Success Rate: Interventional Evaluation of Memory in Vision-Language-Action Systems

VLA 与策略学习智能体与程序学习记忆与技能

首发 2026-10-16；版本：v1。补收原因：近 7 天未推送，针对具身记忆的证据质量有直接诊断价值。  ·  收录于 2026-10-20 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗代码与材料 ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

原文 Reproducibility statement 提供匿名代码与材料入口；本次核验了入口，未运行其复现实验。另需注意：主文 §4.4/Table 2 使用 recorded physical executions 表述，但 Ethics statement 声明全部实验均为仿真、没有物理机器人，二者不一致。下方保留原日报文字，其中“实机”描述需进一步核对。配图由原论文 SVG 渲染为 PNG。 （2026-10-20 核查）

基准／诊断｜VLA＋Agent｜记忆、观测与验证｜桌面操作，含仿真及录制实机执行。

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

When we say that a robot uses memory, does that memory actually play a role? Success-rate ablations alone cannot establish the use of task-relevant facts: they change information and computation together, while aggregate rates can hide offsetting gains and losses. We propose an Interventional Memory Evaluation Protocol (IMEP) for vision-language-action (VLA) systems to address four questions: (1) Does memory provide a net benefit? (2) Under what conditions does memory help? (3) Do changes to memory alter task outcomes? (4) Are these effects specific to task-relevant facts? At the retrieval interface, we compare target-fact substitutions with fact-preserving replacements, minimal numerical perturbations, and exact replicas, while assessing decision correctness separately from motor execution success. We evaluate within-episode, cross-episode, and agentic memory. In cross-episode learned-bank experiments, a one-unit-in-the-last-place (ULP) intervention, including its installation procedure, changes 11.9% of seed-paired outcomes, while changing key facts produces no clear additional effect over fact-preserving replacements. To examine when memory helps, we introduce ChainBench, where correct decisions require historical information unavailable in current observations. The full memory configuration raises task success from 39.1% to 74.3%, matching the oracle-decision condition under shared recorded executions. These results show that correct history can support robot decisions, but establishing whether a memory system realizes this benefit requires fact-specific evidence beyond aggregate success rates.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.text: 通过替换关键事实、保留事实的替换、微小数值扰动和完全复制等对照，区分“记忆改变输出”与“机器人确实使用了任务相关事实”。

docs.title: 关键实验
docs.text: 跨回合记忆库中，极小数值扰动及其安装过程就能翻转 11.9% 的配对结果，关键事实替换未显示明确额外作用。ChainBench 的 202 条两选项任务链中，整理后的记忆记录使决策准确率从 53.0% 到 100%，任务成功率从 39.1% 到 74.3%。

docs.title: 重要边界
docs.text: ChainBench 各条件共享录制执行，使用封存决策／脚本读取，不能当成各系统独立运行的实时端到端实机成绩；也没有证明自主记忆写入已经可靠。没有检出事实特异效应，不代表所有记忆机制都无效。

docs.text:
适合建立评估检查表：今后看到 memory-on/off 的成功率差异，还应追问究竟用了哪条历史事实。

docs.title: Look Before You Act
docs.text:
Look Before You Act: Bridging Active Perception and Vision-Language-Action Models via Observation-Aligned Data Adaptation

VLA 与策略学习主动感知

首发 2026-10-16（v1；补收）  ·  收录于 2026-10-19 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

暂未在论文正文或公开检索中找到可核验的作者项目主页与仓库。 （2026-10-23 核查）

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Robots manipulating objects in clutter must decide not only how to act, but also where to look. Although active camera motion can expose an occluded target, it may move the robot into an initial observation-state distribution that differs from the manipulation policy's training distribution. We identify this problem as first-frame distribution sensitivity: under perturbed starts in LIBERO, naively prepending camera repositioning to pi_0.5 reduces success from 46.3% to 11.5%. We introduce ActiveAlign, a data-adaptation framework that trains a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policy from the states at which active perception terminates. A learned viewpoint module first generates a camera trajectory. Offline, ActiveAlign uses closed-loop alignment to connect the trajectory endpoint to an existing demonstration, replays the remaining manipulation trajectory, and retains successful continuations for fine-tuning. At deployment, the same viewpoint module precedes the adapted VLA without modifying its architecture. Across 40 LIBERO tasks, ActiveAlign achieves 70.7% success with pi_0 and 72.7% with pi_0.5, outperforming their standard-training baselines by 40.0% and 26.4% respectively. Matched-state and data-matched controls support gains beyond prefix shortening and generic viewpoint augmentation; OpenVLA and GR00T N1 also show the same trend. Success rate under physical occlusion in real world increases from 35/90 to 83/90. These results show that active perception benefits manipulation when policy training is aligned with the observation and robot-state distribution induced by viewpoint selection.

docs.title: 关键实验

docs.text: 离线构造数据需要可复位仿真器或可重构工位，100次物理尝试仅保留86条；安全员可中止但不纠正；主动视角仅任务开始调用一次。

docs.text:

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Rapid progress in embodied intelligence has enabled increasingly capable robots to follow language instructions and manipulate diverse objects. However, strong results in structured environments do not automatically transfer to open-world conditions, where clutter, occlusion, and changing viewpoints can obscure the spatial relationships required for action. To address this perceptual gap, a virtual active-perception paradigm is introduced. AWAM, an Active World-Action Model actively plans where to observe and imagines what will be seen along the planned trajectory before acting. Task-related virtual camera motion is predicted and used as a structured query into a geometry-conditioned world model, producing a reusable spatial prior for manipulation, which is later compressed into a fixed memory and fused with live observations through cross-attention for diffusion-based action prediction. AWAM achieves competitive success rates with 75.9% on LIBERO-Occ, 62.4% on LIBERO-Plus, 76.5% on RLBench-OG Occlusion1, and 94.4% in real-robot trials. These results support improved robustness to the evaluated occlusions and distribution shifts, addressing part of the gap between structured manipulation and less controlled environments.

docs.title: HexaShell
docs.text:
HexaShell: A Thin Harness for Exploring the Limits of VLM Agents as Robot Coding Agents

智能体与程序学习记忆与技能

首发 2026-10-16（v1；补收）  ·  收录于 2026-10-19 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗GitHub ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

大系统 + 模块/trick｜Agent / agentic coding｜规划/观测/验证/恢复｜桌面双臂

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Agents built on vision language models (VLMs) now compete with learned policies on robot manipulation leaderboards. We ask how far a coding agent can go when it controls a robot instead of a computer, and where it stops. Our system, HexaShell, keeps the harness thin: it only turns the agent's commands into robot motion. The agent drives a robot with two arms through one command line. It sees three RGB cameras and knows their calibration. After each failed attempt, the agent reads the log, finds the cause, and writes or fixes small programs called tools. In this way it keeps what it learns as code, as a coding agent does when it fixes a failing test. The tools may use only what the robot observes. They use triangulation to find where objects are, relative to each other and to the gripper. If two cameras see the same point, the point lies where the two camera rays meet. If a point lies on a known plane, such as the table or the top of a block, it lies where its ray meets that plane. When the head camera is not enough, the robot moves a wrist camera to get a second view. We build the tools on only ten layouts of one seed per task, then freeze them and test them on ten new layouts of the same seed. We use Codex with GPT-6-Astra at medium reasoning effort. On all 42 RoboDojo tasks, HexaShell reaches a success rate of 39.7% and a progress score of 48.0, averaged in the same way as the leaderboard. This is a new state of the art on RoboDojo. The limit is contact, not reasoning: pushing reaches 92.5% and memory tasks 65.0%, but tight insertion only 8.3%. When the agent fails, it usually sees the failure but cannot make the motion work. We open source the tools evolved so far at https://github.com/HexaFuture/HexaShell.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Geometric and Semantic Foundation models are becoming increasingly popular tools for generating spatial maps for robots. Recent work (e.g., FOUND-IT) has leveraged these tools to construct real-time, task-driven, and open-set 3D scene graphs from a single uncalibrated camera. However, while classical robot mapping techniques have undergone extensive system demonstrations, limited work has been done to develop both the fundamental and the systems wide advancements needed to integrate these new types of robot spatial memory into a full, useable autonomy pipeline. In this paper, we bridge this gap, and in doing so we also evaluate the effectiveness and limitations of this type of 3D memory. Towards this end, we integrate FOUND-IT into a mobile manipulator platform and demonstrate it is well-suited to support multiple objectives such as object change detection, support for multiple mapping sessions, determination of navigable paths, and directly support object grasping for the task of scene re-arrangement. Furthermore, we provide nuanced insights into the effectiveness and limitations of a monocular, foundation-model-driven 3D scene graph construction system using observations from rigorous on-robot experiments. Code is available at https://github. com/MIT-SPARK/FOUND-IT.

docs.text:
PRIME — Not All Actions Contribute Equally: Learning Precise Progress Estimation from Imprecise Demonstrations

VLA 与策略学习

首发 2026-10-16；版本：v1。补收原因：近 7 天未推送，有直接实机精细操作实验。  ·  收录于 2026-10-20 日报

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Progress estimators play an essential role in providing dense reward signals for reinforcement learning in robotic manipulation, but accurately assessing task progress can be much challenging. Existing methods heavily rely on expert data and naively assume that all actions within a demonstration contribute to task success. This assumption often breaks down in real-world scenarios, especially in high-precision manipulation, where subtle geometric errors can lead to task failure. Therefore, these methods can erroneously interpret human mistakes as meaningful progress, further corrupting progress learning. We argue that a key limitation is the lack of a global prior regarding task evaluation criteria, which is crucial for distinguishing meaningful progress from human mistakes. To this end, we propose PRIME, a novel progress estimator capable of learning precise progress estimation from imprecise demonstrations by aggregating experience across trajectories. PRIME constructs a weighted graph over observed states, connecting states across trajectories based on spatial proximity and visual consistency. Edge weights encode spatial distances as transition costs, and shortest-path search approximates the geodesic distance to success. Changes in this distance naturally distinguish advancement, stagnation, and setbacks without assuming monotonic progress over time. Extensive experiments in both simulation and real world on precise manipulation tasks show that PRIME is consistently effective across diverse tasks, and robust to data with varying degrees of suboptimality. Notably, the advantage of PRIME gets more pronounced in higher-precision scenarios, yielding up to a \(5\times\) improvement in policy success rate over the SFT baselines on charger insertion.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.text: PRIME 将多条示范连接为经验图，以到成功节点的最短路径距离估计进度。图源：作者论文 · Figure 3 ↗ · 查看大图 ↗

docs.title: 核心贡献
docs.text: 用多条示范之间的配置与视觉一致性构造到成功状态的距离，让进度标签能识别停顿、回退和无效动作，而非默认“时间过去就更接近成功”；创新在监督信号，不在 VLA 主干。

docs.title: 关键实验
docs.text: PiperX 实机、π0.5 策略，每个任务每种策略评估 30 次。使用含次优动作的数据时，插孔成功率 73.3% 对 SFT 33.3%，困难插孔 70.0% 对 20.0%，充电器插入 50.0% 对 10.0%；后者也高于 ProcVLM 的 33.3%。这是任务成功率。

docs.title: 重要边界
docs.text: 实机是离线进度加权训练，不是机器人在线 RL；在线 RL 证据来自仿真。附录列出 8 万梯度步，仍需示范及机器人配置、多视角信息。每项 30 次，不能把高相对倍数等同于已达到部署可靠性。

docs.text:
GazeAct: Learning Manipulation from Human Gaze

VLA 与策略学习

首发 2026-10-17，arXiv:2610.24507 v1（高相关补收）  ·  收录于 2026-10-21 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

数据 + 模块｜VLA｜感知落点/低层策略｜桌面操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Vision-language-action (VLA) policies must ground language instructions in the right objects, contact points, and target locations for reliable manipulation. Human gaze provides a natural signal for this grounding, but existing robot datasets rarely pair real human gaze with the multi-camera observations used by modern policies. We introduce GazeAct, a gaze-equipped real-robot manipulation dataset and training framework for multi-view VLA policies. Using screen-based teleoperation, we record gaze directly on the robot camera feed viewed by the operator, yielding 12000 demonstrations across 40 tasks and five domains with 300 Hz gaze synchronized with images, proprioception, and actions. We transfer gaze from the operator-selected view to the remaining synchronized cameras, producing spatially consistent targets across the policy's visual inputs. We then use these gaze-derived targets to regularize language-conditioned visual attention during training while keeping inference gaze-free. Across 18 real-world tasks, our method improves average success from 48.1% to 58.6%, with gains up to 25 percentage points. Ablations show that gaze works best as soft supervision and that real human gaze provides stronger attention targets than generic attention-shaping priors. The gains transfer to LIBERO-Spatial (57.9% to 69.6%) and different VLA backbones.These results show that gaze collected in the robot observation space can provide effective training-time targets for improving visual grounding in VLA manipulation.

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Contact-rich manipulation is essential to everyday activities, yet evaluating robots' ability to perform these activities remains challenging because of their diverse contact behaviors and the difficulty of reproducing tasks across laboratories. Drawing on observations of everyday human manipulation, we identify eight recurring skill categories that provide a practical framework for studying these capabilities. We introduce ContactBench 1.0, an extensible benchmark that instantiates these skills through 36 reference tasks and more than 40 object assets. The assets capture task-relevant geometry and contact behavior, support reproducible fabrication using consumer-grade 3D printers, and are paired with simulation models with tunable resistance loads. Controlled task variations enable evaluation of policy generalization. We evaluate recent vision-based and vision-tactile policy learning methods on six benchmark tasks. The results reveal that the evaluated vision-only policies struggle to perceive or react to contact events, while the evaluated visual-tactile policies do not meaningfully improve performance. By providing shared tasks and physical and simulated assets, ContactBench 1.0 establishes a foundation for reproducible evaluation of contact-rich manipulation research. The benchmark is open-sourced at https://jingyi-xiang.github.io/contactbench

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

The Bitter Lesson Comes to Robotics

智能体与程序学习

首发 2026-10-18，arXiv:2610.25287 v2；实质更新 2026-10-21  ·  收录于 2026-10-25 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

本次未在已核验的原论文与摘要中找到作者项目主页或代码入口。配图为评测任务设置，从 v2 原论文 PDF 第 3 页 Figure 1 提取。 （2026-10-26 核查）

基准/诊断｜Agent / frontier multimodal LM｜规划＋低层 waypoint 决策｜真实双臂桌面操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

General purpose multimodal language models (LMs) are increasingly capable of directly controlling robotic arms (e.g., by commanding end effector poses) to manipulate their environment. Tracking the development of these capabilities is important for understanding their potential benefits, such as improving industrial automation, and risks, such as enabling malicious users to produce dangerous chemical or biological agents. To this end, we investigate the ability of frontier multimodal LMs to directly control physical robotic arms. We evaluate nine models at multiple reasoning-effort and service-tier settings on six manipulation tasks taken from the RoboDojo benchmark. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic comparison of a broad range of frontier LMs across a common suite of manipulation tasks on physical hardware. We find that current frontier models can directly control real robotic arms to perform a variety of manipulation tasks but are not yet precise or efficient enough to complete them within a practical action budget. However, these capabilities are improving rapidly: performance increases on our benchmark between July and October 2026 (inclusive) correspond to a performance doubling time of 53.9 days, while the best recorded execution rate increased by a factor of 4.4 and the lowest recorded execution cost fell by a factor of 6.2. These trends raise the possibility that the Bitter Lesson is coming to robotics; the capabilities of embodied general purpose LMs may one day be comparable to those of more specialized models.

来源：arXiv · v2 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.text: v2 将对比从 7 个模型扩为 9 个模型、15 种配置，新增 Gemini 3.6 Flash 与 Gemini 4 Argon 的真机实验，并把趋势窗口从 2026 年 7–9 月扩至 7–10 月。

docs.title: 一句话贡献
docs.text: 在统一真实双臂平台上直接比较前沿多模态模型作为机器人策略时的任务进度、速度与 API 成本，而不是只展示个别成功视频。

docs.title: 关键实验
docs.text: I2RT YAM 双臂、6 个 RoboDojo 任务，每个“模型×配置×任务”20 次，共 15×6×20=1,800 次真机试验，最多 40 个 Cartesian waypoint 动作。最强配置的平均任务进度约 45–48%，但整任务完成仍较少；Gemini 4 Argon 得分 48.4%，却只有 7.1 subtasks/hour。最快的 GPT-6 Astra 为 54.4 subtasks/hour，但约 4.51 美元/subtask；Gemini 3.8 Flash 约 0.38 美元/subtask，却平均约 4.18 分钟/subtask。作者基于 record-setting 配置拟合得到 53.9 天的性能翻倍时间，95% bootstrap 区间为 36.1–59.5 天。

docs.title: 重要局限
docs.text: 这是通用多模态 LM 经结构化工具直接给 Cartesian 目标，不等同于连续动作 VLA；评分由 GPT-6 Astra 根据视频判定“曾达到的最高子任务”，可能高于最终状态成功率。趋势拟合依赖少数 record-setting 点，六任务、固定硬件和 40-action budget 也限制外推。

docs.title: 为什么值得读
docs.text:
它给 agent-as-policy 路线提供了少见的大样本真机横评，并清楚揭示“会做出部分进展”“能整任务完成”“足够快且便宜”是三个不同问题。

VQ-WM: Vector-Quantized World Models for Visual Planning

世界模型与 WAM

首发 2026-10-19，arXiv:2610.25600 v1  ·  收录于 2026-10-21 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

核心方法｜WM/WAM｜高层规划 + 视觉反馈控制｜桌面操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Visual world models have shown strong potential for robot planning, yet long-horizon manipulation remains challenging due to compounding prediction errors, large search complexity, and latent plans that the low-level controller cannot reliably reach. In this work, we introduce Vector-Quantized World Model (VQ-WM), a latent feedback motion planning framework that integrates discrete long-horizon search with continuous visual feedback control: a discrete latent predictor models transitions between vector-quantized latent states, allowing the planner to look far ahead and find a shortest path to the goal through discrete search and a continuous learned controller sequentially reaches the planned states through visual feedback, correcting deviations to mitigate compounding errors. Whereas most vector quantization uses Euclidean distance, we use a novel estimator of the first-passage-time as a quasi-metric, which aligns the planning abstraction with the controller's capabilities. We evaluate on the physical robot manipulation of the Tower of Hanoi puzzle: whereas existing state-of-the-art foundation models (VLAs, WAMs) only succeed when the solution trace in their training dataset, our method achieves 100\% success rate with only short-play data, demonstrate its ability to compose long-horizon solutions beyond the short demonstrated trajectories and execute them reliably. Our solution also outperforms strongest world-models by 13.3--85.3 percentage points on simulation benchmarks spanning manipulation and locomotion, demonstrating consistent progress and new capabilities.

Learning from Fleet Experience: Failure-Conditioned Retrieval and Training

大系统 + 核心方法｜VLA｜策略训练/数据闭环｜双臂桌面操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Experience generated during deployment offers an opportunity for robots to improve policy reliability through learning from their own executions. However, learning through human corrections requires teleoperators to monitor execution and intervene when policies fail, a demand that is difficult to meet as robot fleets grow. We introduce collective experience learning (CEL), a learning paradigm in which deployed robots share their execution experience to improve a common policy. We realize CEL through failure-guided experience retrieval fine-tuning (FERT), which uses failure contexts from robot executions to retrieve relevant trajectory segments from the fleet's shared successful experience and uses their actions as supervision for policy updates, without collecting additional expert demonstrations or corrective actions. A fault-tolerant asynchronous training system (FATS) coordinates experience collection, policy optimization and policy distribution despite local interruptions within the robot fleet. Across five real-world manipulation tasks, the resulting policies achieve success rates of 93.3-99.2%, evaluated over 120 trials per task on robots excluded from training data collection. With collection time per robot held fixed, larger fleets provide more experience and FERT generally achieves higher success rates across the evaluated sizes. On multi-stage phone packaging, learning with 96 robots increases success from 79.2% to 98.3%. These results support collective experience as a practical basis for scalable robot learning and a path towards improving policy reliability during deployment without collecting additional expert corrective actions.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

核心方法｜WM/WAM + VLA｜低层策略/未来预测｜桌面动态操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Dynamic object manipulation requires robots to anticipate target motion while replanning fast enough to avoid executing outdated actions. Existing approaches either rely on fast reactive control without an explicit future target state or encode anticipated motion only implicitly. World Action Models (WAMs) offer a promising alternative by coupling future visual prediction with action generation, but scene-level video objectives may underrepresent target dynamics that are critical for manipulation, while iterative video-action denoising introduces substantial latency. We present TrajWAM, a trajectory-guided world action model for efficient dynamic robotic manipulation. Our key insight is to explicitly ground future visual imagination in predicted target-object motion and use the resulting future representation to condition action generation, while preserving this anticipation pathway after acceleration. Given a short history of object masks, a history-conditioned motion predictor forecasts future masks encoding the target object's trajectory. A lightweight Trajectory ControlNet then steers a pretrained video model toward trajectory-consistent futures. The resulting future representation conditions an action expert to predict executable action chunks. To enable one-step inference without breaking this interface, we introduce a decoupled distillation scheme that combines distribution matching for the video backbone, Trajectory ControlNet realignment, and action rollout distillation to support accurate one-step action prediction conditioned on the compressed future representation. Comprehensive evaluations in simulation and the real world show that TrajWAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on dynamic object manipulation tasks while enabling efficient one-step video-action inference. Project page: https://kevingeng3.github.io/TrajWAM/.

docs.text:
VLDA: Visual Latent Delta Action Models

VLA 与策略学习世界模型与 WAM

首发 2026-10-19，arXiv:2610.25874 v1  ·  收录于 2026-10-21 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗GitHub ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Robotic manipulation is not merely observation-to-action generation, but the realization of task-specified state changes in the physical world. Existing vision-language-action (VLA) methods directly learn observation-to-action mappings, imposing a substantial learning burden due to the gap between semantic understanding and action execution. Although world-action models (WAMs) improve control through future prediction, modeling complete future states wastes capacity on static appearance and action-irrelevant changes. We propose Vision-Language-Delta-Action (VLDA), a paradigm that reformulates full future prediction as compact actionable transition modeling. Its core is a compact Delta variable that captures latent world-state changes, serving as an interface between vision-language understanding and action generation. VLDA learns Delta through a unified objective composed of the Local Transition Filter (LT-Filter) and Global Transition Anchor (GT-Anchor). LT-Filter captures task-relevant manipulation-centric changes while suppressing static reconstruction biases. GT-Anchor provides coarse future-level regularization to preserve the overall direction of state changes. Delta-Driven Action Refinement (DDAR) further grounds Delta in the action manifold and injects it as a structured seed to guide action denoising. We implement VLDA within LoongForge, an open-source training framework for large-scale foundation and embodied models, using its modular and distributed infrastructure for unified two-stage optimization. Experiments show that VLDA improves long-horizon consistency, robustness, and generalization, validating actionable Delta as an alternative to direct action prediction and full future-state modeling.

核心方法 / 模块｜VLA｜低层策略与时间抽象｜桌面操作 + 人形操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Fast and reliable manipulation is crucial for practical robot deployment. Although Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently shown remarkable progress as generalist robot policies, their execution often remains temporally inefficient. A key source of this inefficiency is that policies learn fine-grained temporal patterns from teleoperated demonstrations, requiring many low-level action steps. Temporal action quantization offers a simple way to accelerate execution by aggregating consecutive low-level actions into temporally coarser actions. However, applying action quantization without considering when fine-grained control is required introduces a speed-accuracy trade-off: accelerated actions may efficiently reduce redundant steps in some phases, while discarding critical motion details in precision-sensitive interactions. To address this, we propose PaceVLA, a unified framework for adaptive temporal execution in VLAs that integrates two coupled components: (1) mode-specific action decoders built on a shared action expert, supporting multiple temporal granularities and prediction horizons, and (2) a quantizability-guided mode selection scheme which decides whether coarse execution is appropriate, and a context-conditioned router that selects an execution mode at each inference step. Experiments across three multi-task simulation benchmarks and six real-world tasks show that PaceVLA improves execution efficiency while maintaining task success rate across multiple embodiments, including long-horizon and dexterous manipulation.

docs.text:
ALIGN: Direct Categorical Advantage Conditioning for VLA Policies

VLA 与策略学习

首发 2026-10-19，arXiv:2610.26455 v1  ·  收录于 2026-10-21 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

本次未在论文及公开检索中找到可核验的作者项目主页或代码入口。 （2026-10-26 核查）

核心方法 / 模块｜VLA｜低层策略条件化｜桌面操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Human-collected robot manipulation data often mix successful behavior with retries, pauses, recoveries, and failures. Advantage-Conditioned Behavior Cloning (AC-BC) can exploit such mixed-quality data, but only if the conditioning signal is both accurately constructed from offline trajectories and effectively incorporated into the policy's action-vector-field prediction. Existing pipelines can weaken this signal by thresholding estimator-derived advantage scores into noisy conditions, and by routing conditions through prompts that weakly affect the action vector field. We introduce ALIGN, a condition-aligned AC-BC framework for vision-language-action policies. ALIGN directly predicts categorical pairwise conditions in the policy-facing label space and injects them into a DiT action expert through AdaRMS modulation fused with flow time. We evaluate ALIGN on deliberately mixed real-robot datasets for ARX X5 bowl stacking and Franka key hanging, each combining standard demonstrations with retry-heavy trajectories. ALIGN improves condition fidelity, strengthens conditional vector-field separability, and achieves 90.0% and 56.7% closed-loop success, compared with 56.7% and 33.3% for the strongest AC-BC baseline. These results indicate that aligning conditions from estimation to action prediction is an effective way to extract robust manipulation policies from data in which success, recovery and error coexist.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: 一句话贡献

docs.title: 关键实验
docs.text: ARX X5 叠碗与 Franka 挂钥匙两项真实任务，混合标准与 retry 数据；每个配置固定 30 次。ALIGN 在叠碗上完整成功率 90.0%，最强 ACBC 为 56.7%；挂钥匙 56.7%，ACBC 为 33.3%。

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

The limited onboard computing resources of robots make the inference demands of vision-language-action (VLA) models costly to accommodate. Reducing these demands through aggressive compression, however, can degrade manipulation performance beyond what supervised fine-tuning alone recovers. We present SPAR (Structural Pruning and Action Recovery), which simultaneously prunes the hidden and feed-forward intermediate dimensions of the large language model (LLM) backbone through pruning-aware tuning, then applies reinforcement learning (RL) to recover policy performance. Applied to $π_{0.5}$, SPAR reduces the language backbone from 2.34B to 0.09B parameters and the full model from 3.37B to 1.12B, removing approximately 96% and 67% of their parameters, respectively. At this compression level, RL raises average success across the four LIBERO suites from 84.55% to 93.45%, an 8.90-percentage-point gain. The compressed policy achieves a $1.98\times$ full-policy inference speedup over the unpruned model. These results identify substantial intermediate-dimension redundancy and show that post-pruning RL can recover manipulation performance in compact policies.

docs.text: 最小模型在 LIBERO 上由 pruning-aware SFT 的 84.55 提升到 RL 后 93.45，未裁剪 RL 为 97.70；Jetson Orin 端到端策略延迟 295→148.71 ms，显存 7.098→2.627 GB。真实 AgileX 双臂 6 任务×20 次=120 次，但用的是中等 20% 裁剪配置，成功率 63.33%，未裁剪为 70.83%。

docs.title: 局限

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Humanoid robots hold great promise as general-purpose agents in human-centered environments, yet adapting generalist vision-language-action (VLA) policies to real-world humanoid loco-manipulation remains challenging. Unlike fixed-base or wheeled manipulators, humanoids must coordinate locomotion, posture, gaze, and dual-arm manipulation over a high-dimensional whole-body action space, where inaccurate base or waist motions can easily induce unstable and aggressive upper-body compensation. We propose HAF-VLA, a hierarchical action-flow framework for humanoid VLA control. Built upon a pretrained flow-matching VLA, HAF-VLA inherits the vision-language prefix encoder and action expert weights, and adapts them to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation with learnable stage embeddings and cross-stage KV-cache conditioning. Instead of generating the full action chunk in a single pass, HAF-VLA progressively denoises a shared whole-body action space: first locomotion and head commands, then waist refinement, and finally full-body manipulation. To preserve structural dependencies across stages, we introduce a cross-stage KV cache conditioning mechanism, enabling subsequent action generation stages to refine and augment their outputs based on the action representations from preceding stages. Experimental results across six real-world tasks demonstrate that our framework significantly enhances the performance of existing models in humanoid loco-manipulation tasks, demonstrating an effective pathway for adapting strong mobile-manipulation VLAs to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

Tactile-ETA: Embodied Task Agents Can Perform Fine Manipulation through Tactile In-Context Learning

智能体与程序学习记忆与技能

首发 2026-10-20，arXiv:2610.27613 v1  ·  收录于 2026-10-22 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗GitHub ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

大系统／模块｜Agent｜技能选择、观测与触觉反馈｜接触丰富桌面操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Can embodied task agents use tactile experience to perform fine manipulation without task-specific model training? We investigate this capability through Tactile-ETA, a system that incorporates tactile experience into an embodied task agent through in-context learning. Successful expert demonstrations show how contact changes during manipulation. We pair each recorded robot movement with its camera views and bilateral tactile observations. We keep tactile observations at the start and end of each movement and add two neighboring time points when the tactile images change markedly in between. The agent combines these demonstrations with current vision, tactile observations, and proprioception to select actions through general-purpose robot tools, without updating model parameters. Across four simulated manipulation tasks, adding tactile observations to the same two expert demonstrations increases average success from 15.75% to 24.00%, with current sensing and execution interfaces held fixed. Further experiments show that performance depends on the sensory content and representation of demonstrations, while comparing agent models on Lift Bottle reveals substantial differences under the same system configuration. On the real-robot tasks, demonstrations with aligned visual and tactile observations increase the task success rate from 0% to 60%. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of using tactile experience in context for fine manipulation and suggest a path toward extending embodied task agents to additional sensory inputs.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

RoboCasa-Shift: Stage-Aware Robustness Evaluation of VLAs in Long-Horizon Household Manipulation

VLA 与策略学习移动操作

首发 2026-10-20，arXiv:2610.27861 v1  ·  收录于 2026-10-22 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗GitHub ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

基准／诊断｜VLA｜阶段进度、鲁棒性与失败定位｜家庭桌面操作，含一项移动操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Vision-language-action (VLA) robustness is commonly summarized by aggregate task success, which obscures how individual executions change under distribution shifts and where failures emerge in long-horizon tasks. We introduce \textbf{RoboCasa-Shift}, a diagnostic robustness benchmark built on RoboCasa365 that combines controlled single-factor shifts, matched clean-perturbed rollouts in which each pair shares the same underlying settings and differs only in the target shift, and simulator-grounded stage-aware diagnostics. We evaluate GR00T N1.5 on four long-horizon tasks that pass a predefined clean-performance gate under four perturbation factors and three calibrated severity levels, including conditions that drive the evaluated policy to complete task failure, totaling 1,040 formal rollouts. Robustness responses vary substantially across factors and tasks, and increasing severity does not always produce monotonic degradation. For example, one camera condition yields $Δ\mathrm{SR}=0$ despite 8 of 80 matched episodes changing outcome. Stage-aware analysis further shows that the same end-to-end degradation can correspond to different execution-depth profiles. Camera $L_2$ and Gaussian blur $L_1$ both yield $Δ\mathrm{SR}=0.188$, yet their first-stage failure rates are 19.0\% and 36.4\%, respectively. Our findings suggest that VLA robustness should be viewed as a multi-dimensional property of execution rather than a single end-to-end performance measure, motivating evaluation protocols that jointly capture outcome degradation, paired outcome sensitivity, and failure progression. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/HaochengWang23/RoboCasa-Shift.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

History-dependent robotic manipulation requires task context and interaction history, as the current observation alone is insufficient to determine the next action. Hierarchical frameworks use task memory for high-level subgoal reasoning and low-level policies for execution. However, memory updates require accurate completion assessment: similar observations may correspond to different execution phases, and prematurely recording completion can mislead subsequent subgoal reasoning. We present EventSync, a hierarchical framework that coordinates task reasoning and action execution through event-driven memory updates. A vision-language model generates subgoals from task plans and interaction history, while a vision-language-action model executes them. A lightweight Event Monitor combines visual observations with end-effector trajectories to determine whether the current subgoal is complete. The framework records the current subgoal in its completed-subgoal history and triggers subsequent reasoning only after obtaining completion evidence. With visual history in the executor, EventSync achieves 64.5% overall success on RoboMME, exceeding the best baseline reported in the benchmark by 20.0 percentage points. Further analysis shows that this update mechanism helps build a reliable completed-subgoal history. Experiments on four real-robot tasks with different memory requirements validate the framework's effectiveness in real-world robotic manipulation.

PACT-VLA: Speculative Action-Chunk Verification with Pre-Commit Observations

VLA 与策略学习

首发 2026-10-20，arXiv:2610.28019 v1  ·  收录于 2026-10-22 日报

核心模块／trick｜VLA｜低层策略、验证与异步执行｜双臂桌面操作

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Vision-language-action (VLA) policies are commonly deployed with asynchronous inference in real-world settings, where the next action chunk is generated while the robot is still executing the previous one. By the time the new chunk is committed, the robot and scene have changed, so the chunk is conditioned on a stale observation and task success drops sharply as this inference delay grows. Generating multiple candidate chunks could let newer observations inform the final choice, but existing multi-candidate methods either rank candidates with the stale inference-start observation or repeatedly switch between candidates during execution, which can make the executed action sequence discontinuous. Our key insight is that inference delay can be used as decision time. While candidate generation is still underway, candidate selection can reuse the VLA itself to choose the complete action chunk that best fits a later observation. We propose PACT-VLA, a training-free framework that generates candidates from the inference-start observation and selects one using this pre-commit observation. Its scoring function, FlowRes, measures the residual between each candidate's implied flow direction and the velocity predicted by the frozen policy under the pre-commit observation, requiring no separate verifier. A pipelined implementation overlaps observation processing with candidate generation and batches scoring, so selection adds no control-step delay on the evaluated hardware. At a four-step delay, PACT-VLA improves average success by 15.0 percentage points over RTC on Kinetix and by 5.2 points over single-candidate asynchronous execution with GR00T N1.7 on LIBERO, and it further improves existing delay-robust methods. On three real-robot tasks, it raises average success from 60% to 82% over naive asynchronous execution with the same frozen $π_{0.5}$ checkpoint.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: 方法框架
docs.text: PACT-VLA 的候选动作生成、提交前观测与共享 KV 缓存验证流程。图源：作者论文 · Figure 2 ↗ · 查看大图 ↗

docs.title: 推荐
docs.text: 把异步推理造成的等待时间转化为验证窗口：旧观测生成多个 action chunk，再用提交前的新观测和冻结 VLA 的 FlowRes 选择完整 chunk，不额外训练 verifier。

docs.title: 实验

FIT-MAC: A Closed-Loop Multi-Agent Framework for Robust VLAs

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Vision-language-action (VLA) models have achieved strong performance on standard robotic manipulation benchmarks. However, their reliability can degrade substantially when task conditions deviate from the nominal setting. Perturbations in object positions and task instructions may lead to complete task failure. Existing VLA policies generally lack an explicit runtime mechanism for distinguishing these failure modes and selecting an appropriate recovery strategy. To systematically mitigate this issue, we propose FIT-MAC, a failure-aware, closed-loop multi-agent control framework for improving the robustness of VLA policies at inference time. FIT-MAC augments a VLA policy with an inference-time control layer. First, the Planner Agent parses the language instruction into a structured task specification that captures the manipulation goal and spatial constraints, and the Grounder Agent resolves each instruction-level reference to a visual target. Next, the Verifier Agent tracks phase-specific execution progress, distinguishes target-binding errors from local execution failures, and determines whether intervention is warranted. The Correction Agent then routes permitted interventions to target rebinding or bounded grasping or placement recovery, depending on the failure type. When no intervention is required, the pretrained VLA remains the default action generator. Extensive experiments on LIBERO-PRO demonstrate that FIT-MAC improves robustness across multiple VLA backbones, consistently increasing success rates and achieving state-of-the-art performance under diverse perturbations.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: 推荐
docs.text: 在冻结 VLA 外增加 Planner、Grounder、Verifier 和 Correction agents，将目标绑定错误与局部抓取/放置失败分开诊断，并分别路由到重新绑定或有界恢复。

docs.title: 实验
docs.text: LIBERO-PRO 十类扰动上，OpenVLA+FIT-MAC 总平均 78.7%，OpenVLA 单独为 45.9%；跨底座平均，LIBERO-Object 上 OpenVLA/π0/π0.5 分别由 39.2/42.6/57.0 提升到 85.4/78.4/79.4，Spatial 上由 52.6/50.8/52.2 提升到 72.0/67.4/69.2。

没有真实机器人实验；系统依赖 Grounding DINO、VLM resolver、目标锁、距离和阶段规则等较强接口，提升不能归因于 VLA 本体。错误 grounding 和持续抓取失败仍是主要失败模式；额外 agent 的调用成本和端到端延迟没有形成充分对照。

De-Diffusing WAMs: Action-Sufficient Direct Prediction for Robot Control

世界模型与 WAM

首发 2026-10-20，arXiv:2610.28122 v1  ·  收录于 2026-10-22 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Cascade world-action models (WAMs) use predicted visual futures to condition robot actions, but inherit costly iterative inference from diffusion-pretrained experts. We ask what a single-step predicted future must preserve to support accurate single-step action prediction. In the evaluated WAM, resampling video noise has little effect on downstream actions, yet naively truncating both streams to one step substantially reduces task success. Video-space supervision only partially closes this gap, and a local sensitivity analysis shows that vision prediction errors have highly unequal consequences for action accuracy. These findings motivate DirectWAM, which converts pretrained video and action experts into single-step predictors without stochastic sampling through action-sufficient distillation, while retaining the explicit future-to-action cascade. After learning a one-step action model, we train the future predictor by decoding actions from its own predicted futures and backpropagating demonstration action error through the expert, with an optional future-latent reconstruction loss. The resulting objective evaluates the student-generated future through its downstream control consequences rather than relying on representation matching alone. DirectWAM achieves 97.1% average success across four LIBERO suites and 85.4% on RoboTwin 2.0, outperforming Flash-WAM at the same one-evaluation-per-stream budget. This advantage has also extended to three real-world tasks that we designed. Compared with the full iterative teacher, it reduces inference latency by $28.0\times$.

docs.text: 不再用像素或 latent 重建误差单独蒸馏未来，而让学生预测的未来通过冻结动作专家，以最终动作误差监督未来预测器；保留显式 future→action 级联，但两条流均变为单步。

每项真实任务仅 20 次、每任务使用 50 条演示；LIBERO 的 Flash-WAM 数字来自原论文而非严格匹配 checkpoint。所谓 action-sufficient future 是相对于当前下游动作映射成立，不等于学到了通用物理状态。

Reasoning as a Distribution: Generative Plan Latents for VLA Models

首发 2026-10-20，arXiv:2610.28166 v1  ·  收录于 2026-10-22 日报

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies increasingly reason before acting, but existing reasoning models compress this intermediate decision into a single representation. When several plans are valid, this commitment hides alternatives that could otherwise be selected or revised. We introduce the Generative Plan Latent (GPL), which represents the reasoning state as a low-dimensional conditional distribution over plans, such as which object, grasp, or route to use. This makes the reasoning state addressable: without retraining the VLA, plans can be sampled (coverage), selected on request (steering), and reweighted by deployment outcomes (outcome adaptation). We test all three on SimplerEnv manipulation with $π_0$, and extend the analysis to RoboCasa, LIBERO, and a maze domain. Steering the plan raises the fraction of executions that follow the request from 0.48 to 0.94, while the same guidance on the native action distribution shows no reliable gain. Finally, we show that an explicit plan is most useful when it carries decision information not already determined by the observation.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: 方法框架

docs.text: 将中间 reasoning state 表示成低维条件计划分布，而不是单个向量，使多个有效抓取、目标或路径能够被采样、定向选择，并由部署结果重新加权。

docs.title: 实验
docs.text: 在 SimplerEnv/π0 中，计划引导使遵循指定模式的比例从 0.48 提高到 0.94；直接对 128-D action chunk 做同类引导没有可靠增益。与语言基线比较，GPL 的 steering range 为 +0.54，语言为 +0.02；RoboCasa 离线探针中，重排后 plan-level success 从 0.65 到 1.00。

全部是仿真，大部分多模态场景由作者专门构造；GPL 的总体抓取成功率 0.33，低于语言基线的 0.50。LIBERO 预注册的四项 magnitude prediction 均未达到，且计划接口仍带来 0.274 的基础抓取率损失。
