arXiv v1 的正式题名前缀为 Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids (DASH)。截至核查，原文未给出作者项目或代码入口，检索亦未找到可确认的作者发布链接。 （2026-11-19 核查）

系统＋模块/trick｜VLA｜低层异步控制｜人形机器人桌面取放，仿真＋真机。

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Vision-language-action (VLA) models pair a vision-language backbone with an action head, but in closed-loop control the backbone sits on the control-critical path: while it computes, the robot keeps moving, so each executed action is conditioned on an increasingly stale observation. A larger backbone therefore directly blocks reactivity, especially in humanoid dexterous manipulation. We present DASH, a Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids that removes this coupling. DASH splits the policy into a slow vision-language model (System 2) and a fast flow-matching action head (System 1) that run as concurrent processes over the LCM communication protocol, so the control rate is set by the action head alone, independent of backbone size. The action head fuses stale semantics from a frozen backbone with fresh vision from its own ResNet encoder, desynchronized training exposes it to the staleness it meets at deployment, and an adaptive temporal aggregator aligns overlapping action chunks under variable inference latency. On an asynchronous RoboTwin benchmark that charges inference latency in simulated time, DASH holds 20 Hz control rate from 0.8B to 8B backbones while the synchronous rate falls from 9.7 to 4.1 Hz, with higher success at every size. On a real humanoid with dexterous hands, DASH achieves clearly higher pick-and-place success than the synchronous pipeline.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: 系统架构
docs.text: 慢速 VLM 与快速动作头通过 LCM 异步交换最新值。动作头融合缓存语义和新鲜视觉生成动作块，再经自适应时间聚合交给机器人执行。图源：作者论文 · Figure 3 ↗ · 查看大图 ↗

docs.title: 贡献
docs.text: 将慢VLM与快动作头异步运行，融合较旧语义与新鲜视觉，以错步训练及时间聚合缓解动作延迟。

docs.title: 实验
docs.text: 在将推理延迟计入模拟时间的RoboTwin评测中，0.8B–8B骨干均保持20 Hz，8B同步方案为4.1 Hz；人形真机取放DASH为23/24，同步固定偏移基线为16/24。

docs.title: 局限
docs.text: 真机只测24次取放，且对照同时改变异步机制和聚合器，不能将全部收益归因于异步；人形机器人不等于验证移动底座与机械臂协同。

docs.title: 推荐
docs.text:
关注延迟被真正计入闭环后的模型扩展问题，属于可部署系统设计而非新动作表示。

Thermo-VLA: A Thermal-Aware Vision-Language-Action Model with Gated Residual Modulation for Robotic Manipulation

首发 2026-11-09，v1  ·  收录于 2026-11-12 日报

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have begun incorporating thermal sensing, but existing approaches typically treat thermal images as ordinary visual inputs, providing limited support for temperature-aware relational reasoning in manipulation. To address this limitation, we propose Thermo-VLA with a ThermoRes Encoder, which decomposes thermal images into cold and hot attribute representations and injects them into the RGB token through language-conditioned residual modulation, enabling temperature-driven target selection and continuous manipulation. We further construct six real-world robotic tasks on a dual-arm Unitree G1 platform, spanning basic grounding to relational reasoning. Experiments show that Thermo-VLA achieves an average success rate of 0.86 across four thermal-dependent tasks, outperforming a pi_0.5 baseline that directly incorporates RGB-thermal observations by 18 percentage points. Under unseen-object and scene variations, Thermo-VLA maintains an average success rate of 0.78, achieving the best generalisation performance among the compared methods. Beyond thermal sensing, we transfer the same residual modulation mechanism to colour attributes and observe consistent improvements in both simulation and real-robot experiments, indicating its potential to generalise beyond thermal attributes. Project website: https://j-x-chen.github.io/Thermo-VLA-web/

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: 方法框架
docs.text: ThermoRes Encoder 将热图拆成冷热属性，以语言条件门控残差注入 RGB token，并与文本、本体状态共同输入流匹配动作策略。图源：作者论文 · Figure 2 ↗ · 查看大图 ↗

docs.title: 贡献
docs.text: 将冷热属性分支以语言条件门控残差注入RGB表征，以支持依赖温度的对象选择与操作。

docs.title: 实验
docs.text: Unitree G1 双臂平台构造六种真实任务，每条指令20次；四项依赖温度任务平均成功率86%，比直接拼接RGB与热图的π0.5高18个百分点。相对温度咖啡任务仅58%，说明困难关系推理仍有明显缺口。

docs.title: 局限
docs.text: 需要额外热成像与固定相机标定；使用1307条专家示范，操作员在各试次间重置物体；不是移动操作。简单热选择中相对强基线优势有限，优势主要出现在部分温度关系任务。

docs.text:

docs.title: Bridging Task Planning and Execution for Language-Conditioned Bimanual Manipulation
docs.text:
Bridging Task Planning and Execution for Language-Conditioned Bimanual Manipulation

智能体与程序学习记忆与技能

首发 2026-11-09，v1；补收  ·  收录于 2026-11-12 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

作者项目页提供方法说明和 CENTAURO 机器人实验视频，当前未找到可核验的作者实现仓库入口。 （2026-11-19 核查）

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Robots are increasingly expected to execute natural-language manipulation tasks in real-world environments. This is particularly relevant in household assistance and logistics, where clutter requires reasoning about both task objectives and execution feasibility. This challenge becomes even more pronounced for bimanual humanoid platforms, where coordinating two manipulators introduces additional interaction and kinematic constraints. We present a zero-shot vision-language framework for execution-aware bimanual manipulation that jointly reasons about task objectives and physical feasibility. Planning is grounded in a structured scene representation that combines semantic object relations with execution constraints, enabling the selection of obstacle relocations and execution choices while preserving task semantics. Compatible actions are organised into parallel bimanual stages with explicit pre- and post-conditions. A hierarchical validator evaluates these conditions under perceptual uncertainty and uses stage-level execution history to support local recovery or targeted replanning. Experiments on the CENTAURO hybrid wheeled-legged humanoid robot across nine language-conditioned manipulation scenarios show higher task success than a non-execution-aware baseline. In dedicated failure scenarios, hierarchical validation recovers from execution failures with fewer model queries than always replanning. These results demonstrate the benefits of combining execution reasoning directly into task planning. Videos and additional material are available on the Project Webpage: https://advrhumanoids.github.io/bridging-planning-execution/.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: 方法框架
docs.text: 从结构化场景生成操作计划，将兼容动作组织为双臂并行阶段，再通过前后条件验证与执行历史选择重试、修改动作或重新规划。图源：作者论文 · Figure 2 ↗ · 查看大图 ↗

docs.title: 核心贡献
docs.text: 将对象语义、侧向可达性、双臂并行调度和分层验证连接起来，根据失败原因选择局部重试、修改动作或重新规划。

docs.title: 关键实验
docs.text: CENTAURO 双臂真机，9种桌面场景，每场景相同初始配置重复20次。相对不考虑执行几何的基线，Boxes Aside 成功率0%→85%、Bottles on Box 70%→95%、Long Horizon 0%→50%；Push Failure 15%→95%。同场景二元验证基线分别为75%、90%、35%和85%。

docs.title: 局限
docs.text: 虽为带轮足底座的平台，但所有实验底座静止，不能归为移动操作；20次使用同一初始配置，泛化证据有限。低层依赖既有运动学与操作 primitives，新意主要在规划、调度和恢复接口而非低层学习。

docs.text:
适合拆解 agent 如何把“语义上可行”进一步落实为“机械臂此刻能做到”，并量化分层恢复的收益。

docs.text:
Library of Hands: Fix the Hands, Not the World Model

世界模型与 WAM记忆与技能

首发 2026-11-09，v1；补收  ·  收录于 2026-11-12 日报

补充原文编号 5

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

已核对 arXiv v1 摘要和全文，当前未找到可核验的作者项目主页或实现仓库。配图从 v1 原论文 PDF 第 3 页 Figure 2 提取。 （2026-11-19 核查）

核心方法＋在线适应/记忆｜WM｜规划/观测＋动作接口校准｜以仿真桌面 PushT/机器人放置为主，另含非操作任务。

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

A world model predicts how a scene changes after an action, and a planner uses it to search for actions that reach a goal. If the camera moves or the controller changes, the same command moves the robot differently: when its commands are turned by 90 degrees, a frozen planner with the LeWM world model that succeeds in 77.5% of episodes succeeds in only 7.8%. Current fixes retrain the model, need training data, or forget a set-up when it returns. We propose Library of Hands (LoH), a training-free method that keeps the world model frozen and corrects only the map from commands to applied actions, which we call the hand. LoH reads the hand through the frozen model, with no extra sensor: it finds the action that best explains the change between two camera images (a reading). It stores every hand it identifies, so a returning set-up is recognised rather than re-learnt. In closed-loop tests, LoH more than doubles success on three simulated tasks, from 28.6% to 62.3%, and loses only 0.6 percentage points when nothing changes. It also works, unchanged, with two other world models and on two of three models pretrained on real robot data, and its gain grows with the quality of its readings.

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Tactile sensing is an indispensable modality for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, a capability that hints at the ultimate frontiers of embodied intelligence. However, commercially available tactile sensors are still at a relatively early stage of development, with each type of sensor offering irreplaceable strengths alongside its own drawbacks. A key challenge is thus to free tactile understanding from sensor-specific physics, so that embodied models can effectively leverage heterogeneous tactile data. To this end, we develop LingBot-Touch, a tactile foundation model characterized by the following properties. (i) Our model yields a unified representation across different tactile sensors (i.e., piezoresistive, magnetic, and visuotactile sensors), and is easily extensible to new sensor types. (ii) The resulting tactile tokens are plug-and-play: they can be seamlessly integrated into policy models across paradigms, from diffusion policy to vision-language-action (VLA) models such as $π_{0.5}$ and LingBot-VLA, consistently enhancing manipulation dexterity. (iii) Extensive experiments, spanning simulation and real-robot deployments across multiple hardware platforms, demonstrate that our tactile representation substantially benefits complex manipulation tasks while maintaining strong computational efficiency. We believe the findings in this work demonstrate the potential of leveraging cross-sensor data to scale tactile learning, and offer encouraging insights for the design of future hardware and embodied models.

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

World action models jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language. Existing studies focus primarily on architectures and training mechanisms, typically treating language-video alignment acquired through video pretraining as an established foundation. However, introducing action learning may impair this alignment. Principled guidance on data and supervision design for maintaining language-video alignment during action learning remains limited. To investigate this, we curate a pool of approximately 47,000 hours of general videos, egocentric videos, UMI demonstrations, and robot demonstrations. Building on this, we systematically study how language-video supervision, language-video-action supervision, and the joint use of these two forms affect WAM performance. In particular, we examine how language annotation quality affects pretrained language-video capabilities, and how action supervision from UMI and robot demonstrations extends these capabilities to language-video-action modeling. To better scale the model, we further conduct detailed studies on joint training recipe and model architecture. Under a fixed training budget, mixing egocentric videos and UMI demonstrations improves control generalization. Model architecture affects how effectively these experiences are used, while scaling pretraining under the selected configuration brings further gains. The resulting recipe, post-trained on RoboTwin Clean demonstrations only, achieves success rates of 88.10% and 61.56% under Easy (Clean-to-Clean) and Hard (Clean-to-Random) conditions, respectively. Our model achieves 40.00% SR across three real-world tasks, compared with 23.33% for the strongest baseline, indicating better generalization under unseen conditions. We release the curated data, training code, and model weights.

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights. We build RoboScript, a modular infrastructure that implements WICL for agentic manipulation. From a single demonstration, RoboScript learns each task through rehearsal in simulation, freezes the learned knowledge as a Task Memory, and deploys the frozen memory on new scenes with data isolation that ensures every deployment input is available on a real robot. On all 50 tasks of RoboTwin 2.0, RoboScript reaches 83.4% mean success across clean and randomized settings with one demonstration per task and no gradient updates, exceeding the strongest trained action policy by over 20 points. The method generalizes across visual distributions, improves through reflection, scales with the foundation model, and transfers to a physical dual-arm robot through cross-embodiment memory adaptation. With a world in the loop, a robot can learn a manipulation task in its context as well as it learns one in its weights. All code is available at https://github.com/ArcheOne-AI/RoboScript

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Scene-driven robot autonomy requires selecting tasks from observations as well as executing them. We study scene-driven task formulation and execution under predefined cleaning, safety, and storage/organization categories, without instance-specific goals or action sequences. CAFE maintains online memory of objects, functional zones, and execution states. A rule-guided Trigger-LLM admits formulation from accumulated evidence; Draft, Complete, and Audit propose goals, resolve execution details, and check dependencies. Outcomes update memory for correction and subsequent discovery. Evaluation in 12 AI2-THOR scenes compares three backbones and task-complexity tiers using coverage, constraint, and execution metrics. Tri-LLM records higher GCR scores than the evaluated baselines across three backbones and task-complexity tiers. Controls examine completion, auditing, zones, feedback, triggering, and prompt examples. LimoCobot traces illustrate storage, cleanup, and recovery from a failed grasp. The study examines how shared scene state connects task discovery to execution and outcome-driven revision.

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Robot agents can improve reusable skills, planning procedures, and recovery strategies from execution feedback, yet a fixed practice source leaves the search for new weaknesses unchanged. Useful practice depends on the agent's current capabilities, so the procedure that chooses practice must also be revisable. We present RoboACE (Robot Adversarial Co-Evolution), a framework that jointly evolves curriculum and execution harnesses around frozen foundation models. The curriculum harness uses accumulated capability evidence to propose informative challenges, while the execution harness responds with reusable revisions that expand execution capabilities. Alternating updates hold one side fixed as the other changes, and admitted challenges form fixed snapshots for comparing execution revisions. Starting from a compact set of LIBERO practice conditions, the resulting frozen deployment outperforms the evaluated controllers and agent systems across four LIBERO-family panels. On LIBERO-PRO, it reaches 74.0% success, exceeding the initial deployment by 15.0 percentage points and direct execution by its VLA controller by 13.5 points. Case studies document changes to evidence-guided practice selection, drawer-skill grounding, and controller intervention.

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Reliable medical laboratory automation requires robots to complete entire workflows in protocol order while handling changes during execution. A robot may execute each motion correctly yet fail the workflow by confusing visually similar stages or stalling after human intervention. We present Robo-MLT, a dual-system framework that couples explicit workflow monitoring with learned action generation. A vision--language planner composes an ordered atomic-skill sequence from the protocol and the initial workspace observation. A multiframe execution monitor detects when the active skill has completed or become infeasible, then advances the workflow or triggers replanning. A skill-conditioned vision--language--action policy generates the manipulation trajectories, and an asynchronous runtime coordinates it with the monitor. We evaluate Robo-MLT against four policy baselines and a VLM-based monitor baseline on blood gas analysis and blood sample tube sorting, with 50 nominal configurations per method and 20 sample-removal configurations. Robo-MLT achieves task success rates of 82\% and 70\%, exceeding $π_{0.5}$ by 30 and 22 percentage points, respectively. After an operator removes the sample being handled, the system revises the remaining plan and continues processing the other samples. These results indicate that, under the evaluated conditions, explicit workflow monitoring makes long-horizon laboratory manipulation more reliable and recoverable.

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Vision-language-action (VLA) models now exceed 95% success on the LIBERO simulation benchmark, yet it remains unclear how much of this performance requires generalization beyond the training demonstrations. In this work, we show that retrieving nearby demonstrations and reusing their action chunks achieves a success rate of 91.7 % on LIBERO without policy training. Under LIBERO-Plus perturbations, retrieval shows the smallest drop of all evaluated policies. Across nine publicly available VLAs, fine-tuning mostly makes the vision-language backbone a better retrieval key, and the actions of the VLAs remain close to the demonstrations. In addition, we introduce Local Action Consistency (LAC), an offline metric that measures whether nearby observations in representation space are also associated with similar future actions. We show that LAC tracks the success rate of retrieval and can guide the training of a retrieval key. Our evaluation and source code are available at https://github.com/sereact/lerobot_knn.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

原归档未标版本，摘要采用 v1。

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

This work presents the 2nd-place solution (Team IF1001) to the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge, which evaluates mobile manipulation across 100 household tasks. Our method is built on a powerful world action model (WAM), Cosmos 3. We improve Cosmos 3 by using richer visual history, task-progress conditioning, and task-group and skill-specific LoRA adapters. During inference, we apply a separate progress estimator to supply task-progress context, and use task- and progress-conditioned routing to select a task-group or skill-specific policy, complemented by action-candidate aggregation, rolling inpainting, and task-specific temporal and gripper control. To meet the minimum inference requirement of 1 FPS, we use neither recursive self-improvement (RSI) nor agentic harness methods and rely on no closed-source models; during official private-test evaluation, our system handled concurrent requests across 100 evaluation ports with limited hardware resources, sustaining an average end-to-end inference rate above 2 FPS per port. Our method achieves a mean Q-score of 0.613 and a full-task success rate of 40.9%, averaged over 3 self-evaluation rounds across all 100 tasks. On the official private test set, with 20 instances per task, our system achieves a mean Q-score of 0.615 and a full-task success rate of 41.2%.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: 方法框架
docs.text: 进度估计器从历史视觉与状态预测子任务和阶段，路由器据此选择任务组或技能 LoRA，再由 Cosmos 3 生成动作并闭环执行。图源：作者论文 · Figure 1 ↗ · 查看大图 ↗

docs.title: 核心贡献
docs.text: 在 Cosmos 3 上组合历史观测、进度估计、任务组/技能 LoRA 路由及动作执行修正，构造可在 BEHAVIOR 家庭长程任务中运行的完整 WAM 系统。

docs.title: 关键实验
docs.text: 100项家庭任务，官方私有测试每任务20实例，Q-score 0.615、整任务成功率41.2%；三轮自评为0.613/40.9%。100个评测端口并发，平均端到端超过2 FPS/端口；未用 RSI 或 agentic harness。数据集约每任务200条人类示范。

docs.title: 局限
docs.text: 结果仅为仿真；Q-score 表示部分目标进度，不能当作整任务成功率。该方案是进度与技能路由等系统集成，不是证明所有收益均来自世界模型架构；作者也承认没有逐项隔离所有组件。跨不同年份挑战赛的分数不能直接当作同条件对比。

LaST0.5: A Generalist World Action Model with Interaction-Centric Latent Reasoning

世界模型与 WAM

首发 2026-11-10，v1；补收  ·  收录于 2026-11-12 日报

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

World Action Models (WAMs) have recently emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation, endowing policies with strong capabilities for modeling temporal and physical dynamics. Existing WAMs, encompassing both video-first action prediction and joint video-action modeling, directly transfer global physical representations from world models to action generation. However, global scene representations may underemphasize local robot-object interactions, creating a mismatch between representations optimized for world evolution and those required for manipulation. To bridge this gap, we propose LaST0.5, a novel WAM that introduces an interaction-centric physical representation between world modeling and action generation. Specifically, LaST0.5 learns a compact interaction-centric latent space under the supervision of visual interaction cues between the robot and the environment. This reasoning space is instantiated as a latent expert that bridges the world expert and the action expert within a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture. Furthermore, LaST0.5 performs adaptive world-to-action transfer by jointly predicting future representations and progress values, using progress consistency to adjust action execution and trigger future resampling. Finally, we pretrain LaST0.5 on a large-scale robotic data corpus comprising over 14k hours of data, establishing interaction-centric physical reasoning as a scalable and effective paradigm. LaST0.5 achieves 99.5% on LIBERO, surpasses the previous state of the art on ten evaluated RLBench tasks, and demonstrates robust long-horizon execution and precise dexterous manipulation in real-world experiments.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: 方法框架
docs.text: 世界、潜在与动作专家通过共享注意力连接，以交互线索监督中间潜在表征，并依据预测进度调整动作执行和未来重采样。图源：作者论文 · Figure 2 ↗ · 查看大图 ↗

docs.title: 核心贡献
docs.text: 在 world expert 和 action expert 间增加以机器人—物体交互为中心的 latent expert，并根据预测进度调整执行长度与未来重采样。

docs.title: 关键实验
docs.text: 14,000多小时机器人数据预训练；RLBench 10任务、3种子每任务每种子20回合，平均88.0%±3.0，LaST0为82.0%±3.0，去掉自适应机制为85.0%±2.0。双臂 Tianji Marvin 真机四任务、每项20次且每任务用150条示范，整任务均值63.8%，π0.5为52.5%、Cosmos Policy为43.8%；螺丝插入阶段50% vs 30%，封箱最终阶段30% vs 20%。

docs.title: 局限
docs.text: 每项真实测试仅20次；螺丝和封箱的分阶段指标不可误作整任务成功率。LIBERO 99.5%是训练期间最佳 checkpoint，且基准接近饱和；真实失败包括毫米级孔位误差、摩擦不足与物体碰撞。预测进度在生成未来上是否可靠仍需单独验证（这是基于评测范围的判断）。

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

We study how to generate diverse, physically executable robot demonstrations for dexterous vision-language-action (VLA) learning. Existing demonstration-generation methods typically rely on costly teleoperated examples. Meanwhile, human hand--object datasets provide a reusable source, but existing transfer methods mainly reproduce given interactions. Turning these interactions into VLA training data further requires coverage of different objects and manipulation locations, together with executable arm and finger actions, and visual observations. To achieve this, we present DexSeed, a framework for low-cost generation of dexterous robot data from human hand--object interactions. Our key idea is to expand human sequences while preserving their grasps and realizing the resulting motions under arm-tracking dynamics in physics simulation. Specifically, we organize source sequences by grasp mode with shared language descriptions. InteractionMesh-based retargeting and arm trajectory augmentation adapt these sequences to the robot hand, different object geometries, and pick-and-place locations while preserving local hand--object relationships. An RL finger-control policy produces executable rollouts, while the arm tracks precomputed trajectories. Rendered observations and recorded actions from successful rollouts are paired with grasp descriptions to fine-tune a VLA. Experiments show improved contact fidelity in retargeting and more reliable whole-arm execution than the evaluated baselines. Simulation evaluation and real-world deployment further demonstrate that a VLA fine-tuned solely on the generated demonstrations can execute language-specified grasps. Project page: https://robbyant-research.github.io/DexSeed/.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Foundation models such as GPT and Claude have shown strong capabilities in spatial understanding and embodied intelligence. These advances make agentic robotics a promising path toward artificial general intelligence in robotics. However, we find that using foundation models to control robots poses serious safety risks, and comprehensive safety evaluation is still lacking. We introduce RoboRisk, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating safety in agentic robotics. Its 92 simulated tasks and 13 physical-robot tasks fall into five categories: Task-level Refusal (T), Plan Repair (P), Execution-time Hazard (E), Injection (I), and Sequential Memory (S). Prior benchmarks cover at most two of these categories, and several evaluate only text outputs. In contrast, RoboRisk covers all five and executes every task in closed loop. We evaluate six state-of-the-art foundation models on RoboRisk: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, and Grok 4.7. These models generally show high harm rates. We also evaluate two robot-specific APIs: the Dream API and PokeBot's RoboAPI. We further propose the Lease-Enforced Agentic Safety Harness (LEASH), which offers essential safety infrastructure for agentic robotics and can be integrated into nearly any agentic architecture. LEASH leverages a decision model (Jev or OpenAI's Decisions API) to implement task, action, and commit gates, which review the task, each action, and each irreversible operation in their visual context. The planner and all three gates share a common safety policy. Experiments on RoboRisk in simulation and on physical robots show that LEASH effectively reduces harm across all six foundation models. It largely preserves their task completion performance and adds little time and token overhead.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

World-Action Models improve robot control by predicting future visual dynamics, but iterative video denoising incurs substantial inference overhead. Recent approaches reduce this cost through partial future denoising, yet typically rely on fixed refinement budgets. Our empirical observations reveal that preferred refinement depths vary across tasks and states, while different future regions exhibit varying relevance to action generation. Motivated by these findings, we propose Elastic-WAM, which adaptively allocates world refinement computation across temporal denoising time and spatial future space. A unified spatiotemporal refinement demand field governs when to stop world refinement, how far to advance each denoising step, and which regions to refresh. We parameterize this field with a shared temporal basis and spatial amplitudes, and learn it through a three-stage action-grounded supervised procedure. At inference, the learned field guides recurrent sparse world refinement to improve task success while reducing inference overhead. Evaluations across diverse simulation benchmarks and real-world long-horizon manipulation demonstrate state-of-the-art control performance with reduced inference latency.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

We describe our solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge: 100 long-horizon household tasks in the OmniGibson simulator. We placed 9th on the final leaderboard, the only independent team in the top 10. The core of the solution is a single vision-language-action (VLA) model, one checkpoint for all 100 tasks, built on our 1st-place 2025 solution, which is based on $π_{0.5}$. On the 50 tasks shared with 2025, its Q rises from 0.260 to 0.371; across all 100 tasks it scores 0.392. Our main conclusion from 2025 was that the model was undertrained, so most of the 2026 work went into training the model for longer, optimizing some training parameters, making each training step slightly faster and reducing the gradient noise: a migration from 50 to 100 tasks (semantic stages built from the demonstrations' skill annotations, task and stage embeddings of new tasks warm-started from similar old ones, and a 21-dimensional action space matching the teleoperation controls); variance-reduced multi-sample flow matching with a simple noise-vs-compute model that picks the number of action-expert samples per observation without ablations; and a 200k-step training run, about one pass over the 211M frames of the demonstrations. A cloud evaluation infrastructure keeps a shared record with provenance, episode diagnostics and restorable simulator states, and runs six simulators on one GPU together faster than real time. On top of the learned policy, 14 tasks are routed to a GPT-6 Astra coding agent that controls the robot through observation and motion tools, starting every episode from a frozen copy of its own practice session on training instances. Across these 14 tasks, Astra's mean Q is 0.639, against 0.108 for the learned policy. The public submission included only part of the Astra results and scored 0.446 Q with 27.3% full-task success.

首发 11月10日 UTC  ·  收录于 2026-11-12 日报

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Memory-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) policies are meant to remember what happened. Many of them, however, fill memory by time: they sample frames uniformly across the episode and stamp each frame with its time step. Because time passes even when nothing happens, such a memory may not tell waiting from working. We show that it does not. On the counting tasks of RoboMME, we make the robot briefly pause or fidget its wrist. Such a null event changes nothing the task depends on, yet a released memory VLA counts the interval as work done and stops early. We call this failure phantom progress. It cuts success from 47 to 16 of 50 on one task and from 44 to 10 on the other. When the same frames are withheld from memory, success returns, so the cause lies in memory rather than in the interruption itself. We trace the failure to a temporal shortcut: because demonstrations proceed at a steady pace, elapsed time predicts progress. Indeed, rescaling the time stamps alone makes the policy stop early when the clock runs fast and repeat when it runs slow. Surprisingly, removing the time encoding does not cure the failure, because the frames of a null event still occupy slots of the time-sampled memory. Across RoboMME's released designs, vulnerability follows how memory is indexed. Of the fixes the diagnosis suggests, training with injected pauses does not remove the failure and impairs counting, whereas indexing memory by events recovers half or more of the loss without retraining. A memory meant to remember what happened should count events rather than clock ticks.

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Vision-language-action (VLA) models have made significant progress in general-purpose robotic manipulation. However, sampled action sequences can be ineffective, while evaluating alternatives with computationally expensive verifiers adds latency at each policy query. In this work, we propose HDH, a lightweight framework that uses hindsight from a frozen VLA's own deployments to improve action verification. The framework has three stages. First, we deploy the policy and collect its autonomous rollouts. We then train a compact action verifier to assign each action chunk a predicted task-success score. Finally, the frozen VLA generates action candidates, and the verifier selects the candidate with the highest score for execution. Across four LIBERO-10 tasks, HDH achieves an average success rate of 82.3\% and on three real-world manipulation tasks, HDH improves average success over the baseline policy by 22.6\%.

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Vision-language-action (VLA) models predict chunks of future actions, and when objects move, those chunks go stale before they are executed. We study what makes a pretrained VLA reactive, using \pihalf{} on two dynamic simulation benchmarks and three real-robot tasks. We vary the prediction and execution horizons, compare synchronous and asynchronous inference, test methods that deliver actions sooner or keep successive chunks continuous, and adapt the policy with motion cues and latent-space reinforcement learning. The best prediction horizon is about one second, and the best execution horizon depends on the checkpoint. Short horizons help more with asynchronous execution, and methods that keep the trajectory continuous outperform those that only reduce latency. Adapting the policy repairs targeted failures, but on the conveyor task changing the execution horizon gained as much. Reactivity depends on the execution pipeline as much as on the policy, so both should be evaluated together.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Industrial inspection robots must reach work areas and specific equipment. These destinations span spatial scales from regions to objects, so robots must relate each target to its surroundings to interpret the task and determine where to go. Existing methods support multi-scale navigation through rich environment representations, but at substantial computational and storage cost. These costs limit deployment where wireless coverage is incomplete and robots must rely on onboard computation to keep navigating. We introduce EMS-Nav, a biologically inspired multi-scale navigation framework for online, on-device operation. Its core innovation is to organize perception, spatial understanding, and navigation around regions, making local spaces the basic units of both environmental understanding and computation. EMS-Nav groups objects and their relationships into functionally meaningful spaces and builds a hierarchy from local areas to the broader environment. This organization supports efficient map construction alongside the interpretation and execution of language goals at different scales. In multi-scale navigation experiments, EMS-Nav achieves the highest success rates across all four target categories: objects, rooms, regions, and specific instances. It outperforms state-of-the-art open-vocabulary mapping and navigation methods, improving overall first-attempt success by 9.39 percentage points over the strongest baseline while reducing mapping overhead and language-model input size. Local deployment in real indoor environments further demonstrates its applicability to on-device embodied navigation. By establishing regions as the organizing basis for perception, spatial understanding, and language-guided action, EMS-Nav provides a system that combines multi-scale understanding with computational efficiency to support diverse language goals on resource-constrained robots.

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong performance in robotic manipulation, yet most rely primarily on 2D visual observations and language instructions, leaving scene geometry and obstacle relationships to be inferred implicitly. This limitation is particularly problematic in cluttered environments, where small spatial errors can lead to unintended contacts or collisions. We propose MOSAIC, a modular spatial- and obstacle-aware framework that can be integrated with pretrained VLA policies to improve object-level scene understanding and action generation. Our method augments the VLA backbone with an auxiliary semantic grounding task that predicts role-specific masks for the target object, destination region, and surrounding obstacles. We further combine the target and destination masks with depth estimated from 3D scene reconstruction to construct role-specific geometric tokens that are injected directly into the action expert. In addition, we propose obstacle-aware attention supervision that emphasizes obstacles near the robot body during task execution. The resulting attention features are subsequently injected into later action-expert layers to further guide action generation. Together, these components provide explicit semantic, geometric, and obstacle-aware cues while preserving the underlying pretrained VLA architecture. We evaluate our framework on pretrained VLA model using the RoboPRO benchmark, including visual perturbation tests, and further validate it on real-world manipulation tasks. MOSAIC improves the success rate by 5.1% in cluttered scenes, and by 9.7% under visual perturbations, with gains of up to 25.0% in the most challenging environment. We will release our code and dataset upon acceptance at the following Github page: https://mmahdavian.github.io/MOSAIC/

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Industrial manipulation requires precise alignment and controlled handling of rigid, deformable, and flexible components. Yet, the benefits of pretrained visuomotor policies remain underexplored in settings where limited access to specialized hardware, components, and fixtures constrains demonstration collection and evaluation. Understanding task-specific data requirements is important for assessing their scalability across diverse processes on the factory floor. We investigate whether video pretraining can support reliable industrial manipulation with limited action data. We propose FLUX-mimic, a video-action model, motivated by the potential of video pretraining to capture motion and interaction patterns that enable sample-efficient training. FLUX-mimic is built on a backbone pretrained on large-scale web and industrial task data, and an action expert to generate robot trajectories. We train our policy by joint video-action training. Across four automotive manufacturing benchmark tasks and two bimanual robot platforms, FLUX-mimic outperforms all considered baselines on the dexterous robot platform and matches pi_{0.5}'s average success rate on the gripper-based robot platform. On a deformable part kitting task, FLUX-mimic reaches 77.5% success with as little as two hours of task-specific action-labeled demonstrations.

docs.title: What Can a VLA Learn from the Agent That Calls It? Task-Level Experience Distillation for Embodied Navigation
docs.text:
What Can a VLA Learn from the Agent That Calls It? Task-Level Experience Distillation for Embodied Navigation

VLA 与策略学习智能体与程序学习VLN · 视觉语言导航

首发 2026-11-12，v1。  ·  收录于 2026-11-14 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

已核对 v1 原文与摘要，未找到作者项目主页或实现仓库入口。 （2026-11-21 核查）

核心方法／VLN、VLA、Agent／策略学习与停止判断／VLN 纯导航。

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Navigation agents use a large language model (LLM) planner to call a vision-language-action (VLA) model. Each episode needs the LLM, adding cost and delay. We distill successful agent experience into the VLA instead of distilling the planner. The VLA then navigates alone at test time. Agent sessions are not VLA demonstrations. They include motions driven by planner tools and sub-instructions, along with detours. We present H2E, a task-level experience distillation method that converts these sessions into VLA training data. Every motion becomes a VLA action under the original task instruction, with the resulting poses as targets. H2E masks the loss on steps that move away from the goal. It labels every visited state within 1 m of the goal as a stop. We then update the VLA with low-rank adaptation. The VLA learns to stop at the goal and find goals the base model never reaches. On all 3,189 REVERIE-CE val-unseen episodes, H2E raises the success rate of an 8B VLA from 35.0% to 44.9%.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: 方法框架
docs.text: 收集智能体调用 VLA 后成功到达目标的训练会话，生成路标与停止标签，再微调 VLA 的 LoRA 和路标预测头，测试时独立导航。图源：作者论文 · Figure 2 ↗ · 查看大图 ↗

docs.title: 贡献
docs.text: 把 LLM 规划器调用 VLA 期间成功的导航经验重新标注、过滤并用于微调，让 VLA 测试时独立导航；并非直接蒸馏规划器本身。

docs.title: 关键实验
docs.text: Habitat 中 REVERIE-CE val-unseen，10 个未见场景、3,189 个 episode。8B NavGPT 基线 SR 35.0%、SPL 26.5、NE 8.53 m；H2E 分别为 44.9%、38.4、6.90 m。另一个等训练预算对比中，测地线适配 SR 34.9%，H2E 为 43.2%。

docs.title: 局限
docs.text: 仿真评测而非真实部署；使用四视角 RGB，与部分单视角 RGB-D 发表基线传感配置不同；训练采用 2,395 条 agent 成功会话、额外专家数据以及 9,000 次更新，不能把提升全归因于零成本推理技巧。

docs.text:
HALO: Human-Aligned Data Collection for WhoLe-body MObile Manipulation

VLA 与策略学习移动操作

首发 2026-11-12，v1；补收原因：真机移动操作和数据采集直接相关。  ·  收录于 2026-11-15 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗GitHub ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

作者项目和仓库已核验，仓库提供策略训练、部署及示范视频去手处理代码；数据集、预训练权重和训练检查点需另行准备，本次未运行复现实验。 （2026-11-17 核查）

数据／VLA／低层策略学习与示范采集／移动操作。

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Learning whole-body mobile manipulation requires demonstrations that coordinate bimanual actions with locomotion across extended workspaces. However, existing interfaces trade off direct robot control, perception and action alignment, and natural operator mobility, making such demonstrations difficult to collect. We introduce HALO, a human-aligned data collection system for whole-body mobile manipulation. The system aligns the operator's perception and action space with the robot while preserving direct physical feedback and natural locomotion. Operators guide the robot end-effectors through kinesthetic teaching and move a low-resistance platform without the deployed mobile base while performing bimanual manipulation. This interface enables more natural whole-body demonstrations, but the close human-robot coupling introduces discrepancies between the demonstration and deployment settings. We address these discrepancies with deployment-aligned demonstration processing, which calibrates and temporally aligns platform motion with the deployed base response and masks and inpaints demonstrator hands in recorded observations. Compared with Mobile ALOHA and VR teleoperation, HALO enables up to 2.9x faster demonstration collection while maintaining comparable or higher success rates. Policies trained with HALO perform precise manipulation tasks, including zip-tie fastening, and achieve a 73.3% success rate on a six-stage long-horizon mobile manipulation task involving repeated coordinated base and arm motion. Project page: https://robbyant-research.github.io/Lingbot-ALOHA/

docs.text:
STVLA: Spatial-aware and Temporal-memory for Vision-Language-Action Models

VLA 与策略学习记忆与技能

首发 2026-11-12，v1。  ·  收录于 2026-11-14 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Robotic manipulation often requires both spatial scene understanding and task history. However, many vision-language-action (VLA) policies rely primarily on current observations, without explicitly integrating spatial structure and task history. Appearance-based memories can be sensitive to occlusion and viewpoint changes, while spatial representations of the current scene alone do not preserve how the scene has changed during task execution. We introduce STVLA, a framework that incorporates features from a pretrained visual geometry foundation model into temporal memory alongside visual representations. This allows the policy to recall past scene structure as context for current action decisions. To select informative history, STVLA uses a mathematically grounded scoring rule that balances relevance to the current observation with complementary evidence from memory. Across evaluations on LIBERO, LIBERO-Mem, MIKASA-Robo, and SimplerEnv Bridge, STVLA achieves the highest average success rate among the compared methods on each benchmark. On real-world block stacking, object organization, and phone packaging, it improves success over $π_{0.5}$ by $58.33$, $30.00$, and $35.00$ percentage points, respectively. These results support integrating scene geometry into temporal memory to improve manipulation requiring both spatial precision and task history. Project website: \href{https://stvla.github.io/}{https://stvla.github.io/}

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

Reins: Frontier Multimodal Models Driving Real Robot Arms on Long-Horizon Tasks, Zero-Shot

智能体与程序学习记忆与技能

首发 2026-11-12，v1。  ·  收录于 2026-11-14 日报

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Frontier models such as GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 can now plan and call tools, yet they still struggle to drive real robots through long-horizon, contact-rich manipulation, blind while the arm moves and while they think. We present Reins, a harness in which an off-the-shelf model operates a dual-arm robot with 3D perception tools and atomic actions that report contact and grip. The model chains actions in one call, each with a condition that must hold, stopping at the first that fails; a second instance, the narrator, watches the cameras continuously and reports what changed with every result. From images, Reins also builds a simulation-ready twin of the scene for continual policy learning. With natural-language prompts and no task-specific code, GPT-6.1 Sol succeeds in 88% of real episodes on five tasks; without the harness, it fails every shell game, taking 8 times as long. Three frontier models perform alike but differ in tracking a scene that changes while the actor thinks. Code will be released upon publication.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: EgoX
docs.text:
EgoX: Egocentric Cross-Embodiment Manipulation with Embodiment Dreaming

VLA 与策略学习世界模型与 WAM移动操作

首发 2026-11-12，v1。  ·  收录于 2026-11-14 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗GitHub ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

作者项目与代码已核验。仓库提供 MXT+ 训练、微调、部署与评测入口，数据集和 VR 数据采集管线尚未发布。 （2026-11-14 核查）

核心方法／VLA、WM式潜变量预测／低层策略学习／移动操作＋桌面操作。

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Generalist manipulation policies can benefit from the complementary experience of humans, real robots, and simulated agents. However, differences in morphology, sensing, and control interfaces make it difficult to learn effectively from their combined demonstrations. We introduce EgoX, an egocentric cross-embodiment learning framework that organizes heterogeneous demonstrations through semantically corresponding observation and action modalities. EgoX pretrains a Modularized Cross-Embodiment Transformer with Embodiment Dreaming (MXT+) on this mixture and fine-tunes it on target-embodiment demonstrations. Within each embodiment, MXT+ assigns a dedicated tokenizer to each observation modality and a dedicated expert to each action modality, with a Transformer trunk shared across embodiments. A training-only embodiment-dreaming objective predicts latent representations of future visual and proprioceptive states, encouraging the shared trunk to model each embodiment's dynamics. Across 13 task-embodiment pairs spanning five tasks and six robot embodiments, including five physical robots and one simulated humanoid, cross-embodiment pretraining raises MXT+'s average normalized task progress from 0.63 to 0.80 over training from scratch. The gains are particularly pronounced under out-of-distribution conditions, where average task progress increases from 0.53 to 0.77. Ablations demonstrate the benefits of broader pretraining mixtures, modular interfaces, and embodiment dreaming, with dreaming producing more similar latent geometry across embodiments. Project page: egox-dream.github.io.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.text: 5 项任务、13 个任务—具身组合，覆盖 5 种真机和 1 种仿真机器人，包括 R1 Lite 轮式双臂厨房任务和 xArm7 桌面操作；与 ACT、π0.5 及同架构从零训练对比。预训练相对从零训练，平均归一化任务进度由 0.63 升至 0.80，分布外由 0.53 升至 0.77。

docs.title: ACE-CaP-0
docs.text:
ACE-CaP-0: Real-World Code-as-Policies in the Era of Experience

智能体与程序学习记忆与技能

首发 2026-11-12，v1。  ·  收录于 2026-11-14 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

大系统／Agent、agentic coding／技能与规划验证／双臂桌面操作。

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Recent advances in frontier models have pushed the boundaries of agentic robot control, enabling agents to perform complex robotic tasks through reasoning and interaction. However, repeated calls to these models during execution can substantially increase task completion time. Code as Policies (CaP) offers a route for coding agents to acquire physical skills through experience and retain them in executable programs, allowing the reasoning invested in development to be reused across runs. Developing reliable code policies while limiting the cost of physical experimentation remains a central challenge. We investigate human guidance as a source of priors for feasible actions and simulation as an auxiliary environment for exploring and testing candidate policies. Our findings favor robot demonstrations available on request and simulation used selectively during real-world policy refinement. These findings inform ACE-CaP-0, an agentic recipe that couples policy revision with experience acquisition through Demonstrations on Request and Simulation on Demand. Across eight real-world manipulation tasks spanning alignment, multi-object handling, and bimanual coordination, the resulting frozen programs achieve 92.1\% success (221/240 trials). Mean execution times across tasks range from 0.97 to 2.27 minutes. The programs execute with runtime perception and control, without a human or coding agent in the loop. These results highlight CaP's potential to turn experience into reliable, reusable physical skills.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Embodied foundation models hinge on diverse robot interaction data, which are costly to collect. Egocentric human videos offer a complementary source of experience, and latent action models (LAMs) provide a popular means of leveraging these videos for policy supervision. Compared with world-action models (WAMs), LAMs can offer greater training efficiency and potentially lower inference costs by avoiding explicit pixel prediction during policy learning and execution. However, most existing LAMs learn latent actions solely through video reconstruction, which can cause their representations to cluster by visual appearance rather than by the underlying actions. As a result, they struggle to align human actions with their robot counterparts. To bridge the gap, we introduce SALA, which emphasizes establishing the semantic correspondence for latent actions. Without requiring paired data, we use the language descriptions of unpaired human and robot clips to estimate semantic similarities and supervise cross-embodiment correspondence. Specifically, we translate these similarities into soft neighborhood structures that guide human latent actions toward semantically related robot latents, while robot action reconstruction grounds the latent space in control. The resulting shared latent action space provides a unified supervision signal for training an embodied foundation model on both human and robot videos. Notably, latent action supervision enables scaling along two axes: (1) pre-training on increasing amounts of general human video consistently reduces robot action prediction error on downstream tasks, and (2) post-training on increasing amounts of task-specific human video substantially improves real-world robot task success rates.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Vision language navigation (VLN) is very challenging for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) since small errors in 3D motion prediction can lead to navigation errors and collisions. Unable to fathom execution outcomes in 3D environments, existing methods often struggle to predict accurate navigation waypoints from language instructions. To solve this, we introduce the Prototypical Visual Imagination framework, shortened as ProtoVis-Nav, which forces the model to imagine an outcome-associated local visual representation for the intended next UAV movement. Specifically, we predict feature prototypes and use their linear combination to estimate the visual feature of the target region. In this manner, the VLN model first imagines the local visual representation of the next intended location, and then uses predicted prototypes as context for generating the final action, promoting alignment between visual context and waypoint outputs. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the ProtoVis-Nav framework and show substantial improvements over existing baselines.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

Racing the Clock: Teaching VLNs Budget-Conditioned Object Search

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

A rescue robot entering a building with thirty seconds on the clock should sprint toward the single most promising room; given ten minutes, it should instead explore a broader tour. Yet vision-language-navigation (VLN) models are typically evaluated under a fixed episode limit that the policy never observes, even though time-critical missions require behavior to adapt to the available budget. We study budget-conditioned object search: given a target category and an explicit action budget, an agent must find as many distinct target instances as possible before the budget expires. We investigate how to supervise VLNs for this task by comparing a privileged TSP expert, which plans near-optimal routes using the full map and true target locations, with a room-level Bellman expert that maximizes expected return under partial observability using high-level cross-scene semantic priors. Despite the TSP expert achieving substantially higher expert performance, its demonstrations are less effective for learning exploration: on held-out HM3D scenes, the Bellman-supervised VLN consistently outperforms the TSP-supervised VLN, with the advantage becoming more pronounced at longer budgets. At 2000 steps (500m), the Bellman-supervised VLN finds 71.4% of reachable target instances, compared with 65.5% for the TSP-supervised VLN and 44.8% for the pretrained VLN. These results highlight a distinction between optimal routing and optimal exploration: effective exploration supervision should optimize decisions under partial observability rather than imitate routes that are optimal only once the environment is fully known.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.text: 房间级 Bellman 专家按已探索信息与剩余预算估值前沿房间，执行中遇到目标可中断扫描并重新规划。图源：作者论文 · Figure 2 ↗ · 查看大图 ↗

docs.title: 贡献
docs.text: 让视频 VLN 从房间级 Bellman 专家示范中学习根据剩余动作预算调整多目标搜索，而不是改变低层网络结构。

docs.title: 实验
docs.text: Habitat 的 HM3D 十个未见场景、每种预算 100 个匹配 episode；预算 400 步时，找到的有效目标比例 58.0%，原始 Uni-NaVid 为 35.5%，对象级专家训练为 45.0%。预算 2000 时分别为 72.7%、44.8%、65.5%，但直接执行、具有显式记忆的 greedy frontier 达 93.8%。真实四足在同一住宅找 14 把椅子，预算 50 和 2000 下各 5 次试验，平均找到 3.4 和 9.2 把。

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Long-horizon navigation from indoors to outdoors remains an open problem for humanoid robots: one instruction covers rooms, doors and roads, and the camera moves with the gait. Worken, AGIBOT's measure of productive robot work, depends on robots that reach their workplaces autonomously. We present X-Nav, to our knowledge the first system to take a bipedal humanoid through a language-instructed long-horizon mission from indoors to outdoors. X-Nav covers a pipeline from data to deployment. Its data engine collects navigation data in open-source scenes, in digital twins of deployment sites and on real robots. Its navigation model, MELIOR, takes only RGB images from the robot's built-in camera and comes in two versions: MELIOR-A predicts actions, and MELIOR-N predicts a navigation goal. Its agentic workflow, X-Navarch, turns a brief human instruction into sub-tasks and deploys MELIOR on the robot with explicit target navigation and obstacle avoidance. On the Lingxi X2, X-Nav completes a mission of about a hundred metres from an office lobby to a store in a neighbouring building; LiDAR and odometry are used for target approach and low-level control. The mission is completed with both versions of MELIOR: the robot follows a change of destination and walks through a door from the lobby to the road, and with X-Navarch it also passes static and dynamic obstacles on the route. During deployment, MELIOR is adapted with data collected in a digital twin of the site; the adaptation raises its closed-loop success rate in the twin, and the adapted model is then deployed on the robot at the real site. In addition, MELIOR achieves competitive results on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE benchmarks.

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Joint world action models (WAMs) generate future actions and states together, modeling world-action trajectories rather than actions alone. However, trajectory imitation does not ensure that these trajectories are task-effective or consistent with dynamics. We present \textbf{world action trajectory optimization (WATO)}, which optimizes generated actions and future states jointly for control. WATO uses both as references in a dynamics-constrained trajectory optimization problem and differentiates the task loss through the optimized trajectory to train the generator. This makes generated trajectories task-aware and dynamics-consistent while using trajectory optimization only during training. At deployment, WATO directly generates candidate trajectories and ranks them with a world model, without iterative trajectory optimization. Across $7$ visual control environments, WATO improves average success from $79.9\%$ for the imitation joint WAM to $91.7\%$, outperforming strong model-based, goal-conditioned RL, and generative control baselines. Compared with cross-entropy method (CEM), WATO is on average $11.5\times$ faster and uses $600.5\times$ fewer world model evaluations at deployment.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Independently pretrained language models and vision-language-action (VLA) policies provide complementary building blocks for embodied agents, but connecting them does not automatically produce coordinated behavior. The VLA may generate actions that diverge from the LLM's intended subtask and, upon regaining control after a correction, undo the promising state restored by the LLM. We introduce ESI (Embodied Self-Improvement), an automated flywheel that uses environmental interaction to align reasoning and action. ESI treats the modular agent as the unit of post-training, repeatedly refining the prompts that guide the LLM, the shared skill interface that expresses its intent, and the VLA parameters that realize that intent, then redeploying these components together. Our key insight is that collaboration itself can supply supervision for improving this interface. The LLM's subtask decisions provide semantic supervision for what the policy should execute, while its effective corrections and subsequent student continuations provide action-level supervision for recovery and handoff. The student also learns from its own effective execution, allowing locally useful experience to contribute even when the overall episode fails. On ten selected RoboDojo tasks, ESI achieves a mean Score of 62.03 and a mean success rate of 49.41% using an LLM-VLA agent without generating task-specific control code. On both metrics, it outperforms the published reference results of all hybrid embodied agents, including the Agent+WAM system GO-3 Nano Preview (47.27 Score and 36.60% success), as well as all compared code-based methods.

docs.text: LLM 规划与纠错、VLA 执行共同产生经验，再分路更新决策提示、技能目录和 VLA 策略。图源：作者论文 · Figure 2 ↗ · 查看大图 ↗

docs.title: 局限

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Accessible mobility is user-conditioned rather than scene-intrinsic, as walkable paths for one embodiment are inaccessible to another. Yet, existing benchmarks evaluate traversability under a fixed and limited embodiment. We present Vision-Language Accessible Navigation (VLAN), containing 1,000 scenes, 20K navigation trajectories, and 160K keyframes across diverse lighting, environmental conditions, scene semantics, and path geometries. For each trajectory, VLAN provides embodiment-specific actions and accessibility features for legged and wheeled agents, including humanoid and quadruped robots and people with visual or mobility impairments, while everyday obstacles and accessibility labels are categorized as Passable, Bypass, HighRisk, and Blocked. Unlike goal-only evaluation, our benchmark measures physical safety and alignment with user-specific constraints via goal-reaching, collision-aware, and accessibility-aligned metrics. We benchmark modern vision-language models and find they often fail to consistently adapt obstacle relevance, path selection, and safety criteria across user profiles, suggesting accessibility-aware navigation requires dedicated datasets, tasks, and metrics beyond conventional embodied navigation evaluation. All data and code open-source at https://github.com/InSAI-Lab/VLAN.

docs.title: ReRead
docs.text:
ReRead：阶段歧义下复用策略历史缓存

记忆与技能

首发 11 月 16 日 arXiv v1  ·  收录于 2026-11-20 周报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

原文及周报所列作者代码与权重链接 https://github.com/tan2355/reread 经两次访问均返回 HTTP 404，当前不列作可用实现入口；周报正文中的原链接与原表述予以保留。 （2026-11-22 核查）

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

When a pretrained robot policy fails on challenging tasks, common remedies include retraining the backbone, adding an external visual encoder, or introducing a memory module. We argue that wrong predictions do not imply wrong representations: a policy can retain the required information yet fail to read it out as the correct action. To test this view, we propose ReRead: with the backbone frozen, a corrector re-reads the current and two previous caches to predict an action residual. The corrector sees no images, is trained solely on offline demonstrations from all 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, and adds only 4.17% latency. Ablations and interventions show that the correction relies on the backbone's own representations: none of four external visual encoders adds further gain, and swapping in past caches from other trajectories sharply increases action error. On the 11 hardest RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, ReRead improves the success rates of LingBot-VLA, $π_{0.5}$, and Fast-WAM by 23.45, 13.09, and 8.00 percentage points, respectively. In paired evaluation on all 50 tasks, it raises Fast-WAM's average success rate from 90.73% to 92.66%. On a Flexiv dual-arm robot, it raises success on a phase-ambiguous task from 0% to 36%.

docs.text: Flexiv 双臂阶段歧义任务成功率从 0% 到 36%；这是单类任务，不能据此推断对多种接触任务的泛化。作者报告额外延迟 4.17%，其具体硬件和测量口径应按论文复现。

docs.title: TaF-Foundation
docs.text:
TaF-Foundation: Wrench-Grounded Cross-Sensor Tactile Representations

其他具身方向

首发 2026-11-16，v1。  ·  收录于 2026-11-18 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Tactile sensing is essential for contact-rich manipulation, yet heterogeneous sensing mechanisms and observation formats hinder cross-hardware transfer. Since physical contact is governed by Newtonian mechanics, we ground tactile representations in six-dimensional wrenches, establishing a common physical reference across sensing mechanisms. Specifically, we pair tactile observations from all sensors with wrench measurements, enabling shared physical supervision without requiring direct tactile-to-tactile pairing between sensors. To support learning at scale, we develop a dedicated acquisition platform and collect over 100 million paired tactile observations and wrench measurements from 24 sensors spanning four families of sensing principles. Building on this dataset, our framework combines sensor-specific input adaptation with a shared tactile encoder. By learning to reconstruct wrenches, the encoder maps observations from different sensors into a shared, continuous feature space grounded in contact physics. To leverage these representations for manipulation, we introduce TaF-Policy, which integrates tactile features with visual observations and robot states to generate action chunks. We evaluate the learned representations through wrench estimation, cross-sensor retrieval, few-shot adaptation to unseen sensors, and robotic manipulation. On the core benchmark, our method reduces single-frame force RMSE by 17.1% and improves cross-sensor retrieval R@1 by 13.11 percentage points over the strongest baseline. In manipulation experiments, TaF-Policy achieves average success rates of 51.33% across three simulated tasks and 46.25% across four real-world tasks, compared with 47.33% and 23.75%, respectively, for the strongest baselines evaluated on the same task sets. Project page: https://mrjiangjm.github.io/TaF-Foundation/.

docs.text: PAPER NOTE · 精选 05

docs.title: ACiT
docs.text:
ACiT: Proprioceptive-Prior Action Chunking with Inverted Transformers

VLA 与策略学习

首发 2026-11-16，v1。  ·  收录于 2026-11-18 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

未在已核验的 v1 摘要与正文中找到作者项目主页或实现仓库入口。 （2026-11-22 核查）

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Visuomotor policies condition action prediction on visual and proprioceptive observations. While historical proprioceptive sequences carry rich dynamic priors, current methods treat them as equal to high-dimensional vision, causing the proprioceptive signal to be overwhelmed. To identify what is lost in equal-conditioning fusion, we analyze proprioceptive data and find that strong inter-joint coupling is the key action-determining structure. This finding aligns with the neural sensorimotor loop, in which proprioception first forms a body-centered prior and vision is later calibrated via parietal remapping. Inspired by this, we propose ACiT, Proprioceptive-Prior Action Chunking with Inverted Transformers, which reinforces historical joint-coupling as the primary condition with vision as a later calibration. This design is instantiated through three modules: Inverted State Encoding builds a proprioceptive prior via per-joint tokens and inter-joint self-attention. State-Visual Grounding lets joint tokens query visual evidence, making vision goal- and calibration-only. Inverted Action Chunking decodes per-joint trajectories independently. ACiT improves success rates on most LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world tasks, with the largest gains on those that require dynamics and coordination. The same conditioning design transferred to the VLA backbone pi_0-ACiT yields significant gains with better execution efficiency.

WiTac: Wrist-Informed Tactile Representations for Contact-Rich Manipulation

VLA 与策略学习

首发 2026-11-16，v1。  ·  收录于 2026-11-18 日报

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Similar tactile contacts can call for different corrections depending on the configuration of the hand, object and target. Rather than supplying touch and wrist vision separately, fusing them before policy injection better grounds tactile features in visual context, yielding more accurate contact representations. We introduce Wrist-Informed Tactile Representations (WiTac), a pretrained encoder that learns such representations before action generation. Pretrained on nearly 300 hours of SharpaDex data, WiTac deeply fuses tactile signals with hand motion and wrist views into a comprehensive contact representation. Conditioning downstream VLA policies (GR00T N1.7 and $π_{0.5}$) on WiTac substantially improves task success over vision-only base policies across four contact-rich manipulation tasks (+28.8% and +15.0% on average), and further outperforms a wrist-free tactile encoder by 18.8% and 7.5%, respectively. Offline analyses further show that incorporating wrist vision yields more accurate contact descriptors, stronger joint task-contact discrimination, greater feature stability under tactile noise, and clearer action-direction readout from similar contacts.Project page: https://wrist-informed-tactile-representations.github.io/.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.text: PAPER NOTE · 精选 02

docs.title: ForceHarness
docs.text:
ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models

智能体与程序学习记忆与技能

首发 2026-11-16，v1。  ·  收录于 2026-11-18 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗GitHub ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

作者项目与仓库提供接触原语、力估计、MuJoCo 和 ForceBench 仿真及 Franka 部署接口；运行需分别配置机器人或仿真环境与模型服务，本次仅核验资源。 （2026-11-19 核查）

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Frontier multimodal models can now control robots zero-shot from images, yet many manipulation tasks depend on contact forces that images cannot show. Bringing force to an API-only frozen model raises two challenges. First, contact evolves much faster than an API model can decide, so the system must close the loop on force beneath the model. Second, a frozen model cannot interpret raw force streams, so force must be returned in a form the model can reason about. Therefore, we present ForceHarness, a harness that lets frozen models use force without demonstrations or finetuning. After calibrating hand force from a wrist sensor or joint torques alone, ForceHarness addresses the first challenge with self-terminating force primitives that regulate force on their own and return at a contact event. To address the second challenge, a physics translation layer turns each force trace into physical quantities with uncertainty as the tool result. To evaluate ForceHarness against expert force controllers and learned policies under identical conditions, we also build HiddenPhys, a seven-task MuJoCo benchmark with hidden physical variables. On a real arm without a wrist force sensor, ForceHarness raises the zero-shot success rate of GPT-6 Astra from 3.3% to 90.0%. In simulation, it adds 17.5 percentage points on the public ForceBench suite and 34.3 percentage points on HiddenPhys, surpassing force-aware policies trained on demonstrations on both benchmarks and matching hand-written expert controllers on HiddenPhys. Ablations further show that smaller models make significantly better decisions when given physical quantities rather than raw force values.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.text: PAPER NOTE · 精选 01

docs.title: ReuseMem
docs.text:
ReuseMem：动作价值监督的多目标记忆检索

记忆与技能

首发 11 月 16 日 arXiv v1  ·  收录于 2026-11-20 周报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

未在已核验的 arXiv v1 摘要和正文中找到可核验的作者项目主页或实现仓库入口。 （2026-11-22 核查）

直接相关：上下文价值估计、检索与缓存

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Robots that work alongside people should be able to use what they have seen when new requests arise. The same experience may later support identifying an object or returning it to its original location, although these uses were unknown during observation. ReuseMem learns to use one visual memory for multiple later manipulation goals. It records visual features independently of future goals, retrieves complementary evidence for each request, and combines it with the current scene through a lightweight action interface. Retrieval is supervised by how well candidate evidence supports expert-action prediction across different current states, linking memory selection to its use in manipulation. Repeated visual features are stored once, and memory computations that remain unchanged during action generation are reused. Experiments on four simulation tasks and two physical scenarios demonstrate reuse of a common recording across different requests. With matched action adaptation, ReuseMem improves joint goal completion on the benchmark tasks by 24.5 percentage points over uniform memory. These findings show that one memory can support multiple later manipulation goals as the scene changes.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: 方法框架
docs.text: 目标无关的 Writer 对重复视觉表征共享存储，为每次观察保留独立时间记录；Reader 按请求检索互补历史，经当前场景融合后供冻结动作策略使用。图源：作者论文 · Figure 2 ↗ · 查看大图 ↗

docs.title: 方法
docs.text: 目标无关地保存视觉历史；Reader 针对请求选择互补证据，以候选历史在多个当前状态下对专家动作预测的支持程度监督选择；冻结预训练策略，通过融合与低秩适配利用历史。重复视觉特征共享存储，并缓存不变的记忆投影。它的记忆主要是过去场景观察，不是与你的示范动作邻居完全相同的检索对象。

docs.title: 仿真闭环
docs.text: 四个任务、200 条共同记录，All-goal（对每个记录两个独立分支均成功）从匹配动作适配的 uniform memory 36.0% 升至 60.5%；不重置的 Sequence 从 35.0% 升至 58.0%。去掉检索学习为 36.5%，单状态监督为 53.0%，完整多状态监督为 60.5%；去掉当前场景融合后分别为 All-goal 55.5%、Sequence 47.0%。这些结果支持所测任务中的证据选择与当前场景融合，不证明在线刷新收益。

docs.title: 真实机器人
docs.text: SO101 两个桌面场景，每场景 20 条记录；方法在各场景的三目标独立分支均成功为 14/20，连续序列成功为 13/20。任务侧重历史身份、位置和场景变化，不能视为阶段转移或接触丰富操作的专门验证。

docs.title: 开销
docs.text: RTX 5090、BF16、batch 1 下，新请求到首条命令 175 ms，uniform memory 为 163 ms；同目标延续时缓存将响应从 174 ms 降至 165 ms。2,048 条时间记录下共享表征占 43.98 MiB，对照为 66.38 MiB。这里的 12 ms 差异是完整路径差值，不能当作纯检索耗时。原文未找到可核实的作者代码链接。

docs.title: 局限及 WHEN 联系
docs.text:
论文按请求检索并复用计算，没有对同一动作阶段内何时刷新做受控实验；视觉匹配、精细操作及历史/目标范围有限。可借鉴动作条件效用替代纯距离，但监督需要专家动作，其部署时的近似方式仍须另行验证。

docs.title: Cooperative Mobile Manipulation using Learned Dynamical Systems
docs.text:
Cooperative Mobile Manipulation using Learned Dynamical Systems

记忆与技能移动操作

首发 2026-11-16，v1。  ·  收录于 2026-11-19 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

原文提供演示视频，但未在已核验的 v1 摘要与正文中找到作者项目主页或实现仓库；未把视频链接列作代码入口。 （2026-11-22 核查）

核心方法／其他：动力系统与多机器人规划（非 VLA、非 VLN）／技能协调与低层控制／双移动机械臂操作。

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Cooperative mobile manipulation requires robots to coordinate their motions while ensuring whole-body collision avoidance and preserving task-relevant behaviors. We propose CALDS (Cooperative Adaptation of Learned Dynamical Systems), a framework that enables mobile manipulators to adapt learned single-agent behaviors for coordinated execution. Building on individual dynamical systems (DSs) learned from demonstrations, CALDS enables cooperative adaptation through two key components: Cooperative Policy Selection, which identifies compatible combinations of learned policies, and Temporal Adaptation, which ensures collision-free cooperation while preserving the spatial structure and convergence properties of the original behaviors. We evaluate CALDS across three diverse scenarios: assistive dressing, restaurant cleaning and serving, and drawer opening and object placement. Quantitative results demonstrate its effectiveness in improving task success and enabling safe, coordinated simultaneous execution while maintaining fidelity to demonstrated behaviors.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: 方法流程
docs.text: 从单机器人示范学习动力系统，按合作任务选择策略组合，再调整时序以满足任务顺序和全身避碰约束。图源：作者论文 · Figure 1 ↗ · 查看大图 ↗

docs.text: 在单机器人示范学习出的动力系统基础上，选择兼容策略并做时间调整，以协调两个移动机械臂、避碰并保留轨迹形状。

docs.title: 实验
docs.text: 仿真中每台机器人由 Dingo 全向底座和 Kinova Gen3 Lite 组成，穿衣辅助、餐桌清洁服务及抽屉取放三场景，每场景 200 组随机初始条件；两种 CALDS 变体整体成功率 91%–100%。有状态噪声且规划上限 1 秒时，一种变体在餐厅场景从 91% 降至 79%。

docs.title: 局限
docs.text: 纯仿真，没有 VLA 语言理解或真机部署；动作查询约 0.18ms 不等于完整规划延迟，平均规划约 0.76 秒（另一变体约 1.49 秒），不应宣称端到端 10–100Hz。

docs.title: ScaleVLA
docs.text:
ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters

VLA 与策略学习

首发 2026-11-16，v1。  ·  收录于 2026-11-18 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗GitHub ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

作者项目与仓库已核验，提供数据准备、特征提取、训练、服务与仿真闭环评测入口；骨干模型、动作模型与数据需另行获取，本次未运行复现实验。 （2026-11-19 核查）

核心方法／VLA／低层策略学习／双臂桌面操作。

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. Yet most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies still rely on much smaller VLM backbones, leaving this potential largely untapped. We ask whether frontier-scale representations can provide a stronger foundation for robot learning. We introduce ScaleVLA, which connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT, and systematically compare VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup. We evaluate three fundamental capabilities of robot foundation models. In sample efficiency, just 10 demonstrations outperform a 2B backbone trained with 50 (87.8% vs. 85.6%). In generalization, LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1%, compared with at most 31.3% for smaller backbones. In precise manipulation, real-world charger insertion improves from 4/10 to 9/10 successes, with gains concentrated in contact-sensitive alignment. Despite its scale, ScaleVLA achieves 216 ms median latency per action chunk. Our findings suggest that frontier VLMs can serve not only as reasoning agents, but also as powerful representational foundations for efficient and generalizable robot policies.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.title: 方法框架
docs.text: 视觉语言骨干编码图像和指令，特征适配器与机器人状态连接动作 DiT，通过流匹配生成动作块。图源：作者论文 · Figure 2 ↗ · 查看大图 ↗

docs.title: 贡献
docs.text: 以 552B 稀疏 MoE 视觉语言骨干连接动作扩散 Transformer，在统一动作头和数据条件下研究骨干规模，骨干用特征而非逐字推理。

docs.title: 实验
docs.text: 双臂真实充电器插接，域内 ScaleVLA 9/10，2B Cosmos 基线 4/10，π0.5 骨干 8/10；OOD 分别 8/15、5/15、7/15。LIBERO-PRO 成功率 45.1%，较小骨干最高 31.3%。

docs.title: 局限
docs.text: 真机仅一项任务、小样本，9/10 对 8/10 不足证明稳健优越；真实训练含完整遥操作和额外插接片段。摘要的 216ms 是四张 H200 上 RoboCasa 的每动作块中位数；真机客户端往返中位数为 384ms，不能混为一谈。

docs.text:

docs.title: Hidden Variables Behind Real-Robot Data Quality
docs.text:
Hidden Variables Behind Real-Robot Data Quality: Lessons from Hundreds of Thousands of Hours

VLA 与策略学习

首发 2026-11-17，v1。  ·  收录于 2026-11-19 日报

论文原文 ↗PDF ↗项目主页 ↗中文翻译 ↗返回本期目录

已核验原文所列作者团队遥操作系统主页；该页面为系统介绍，当前未找到对应报告的公开实现入口。HTML 缺失概览图，配图从 v1 原 PDF 第 1 页直接提取，保留原始位图。 （2026-11-22 核查）

数据、诊断／VLA、模仿学习／数据采集与低层策略学习／双臂操作及移动采集。

docs.title: Abstract · 摘要原文
docs.text:
复制原文

As real-robot data collection scales, collection-system design shapes both operator efficiency and the behaviors learned by robot policies. Workspace limitations, control-interface friction, and latency can introduce pauses, detours, and corrective motions into otherwise successful demonstrations. We investigate these effects across embodiment, teleoperation control, and data consistency, combining a kinematic study of 25 dual-arm robots, controlled teleoperation experiments, and real-robot evaluation of fine-tuned $π_{0.5}$ policies. The embodiment study shows that positional reachability overstates orientation-aware task coverage and that modest shoulder motion can substantially expand the effective workspace. Teleoperation experiments show that parallelizing body-part control reduces task completion time by 43-53%, while compliant control improves success and reduces peak contact forces on constrained and contact-rich tasks. Policy-learning experiments show that demonstrations must capture the visual information underlying action choices: active-search demonstrations improve arm-selection accuracy from chance (50%) to 100%. Calibration experiments reveal that mixed-calibration training data remain usable in our tested configurations when an inference-aligned subset is retained, whereas inference-time miscalibration causes all 30 trials to fail. Policies also retain approximately 90% of the extra path length in detour-contaminated demonstrations, showing how inefficient operator motions persist in learned behavior. Together, these findings connect collection-system design to demonstration quality and downstream policy execution. They motivate evaluating effective workspace, control efficiency, observation completeness, calibration alignment, and motion quality before scaling collection, and addressing system-induced compensations at their source.

来源：arXiv · v1 ↗展开全文 ↓

docs.text: 原论文概览展示具身设计、遥操作控制与数据质量如何连接示范采集和机器人策略学习。图源：作者论文 · Figure 1（PDF 第 1 页） ↗ · 查看大图 ↗
